body:
I'm encountering a SyntaxError in my React application when trying to parse JSON data. The error message is:

SyntaxError: "[object Object]" is not valid JSON
    at JSON.parse (<anonymous>)
    at onClick (UserStatusModal.js:480:1)

This error occurs when I'm trying to parse session data like this:

JSON.parse(session?.summary_data ?? JSON.stringify({}))

The session data is fetched from an API and I'm not sure about its exact format. How can I make this code more robust to handle different data types and prevent this error?

This error occurs because you're trying to parse a string representation of an object ("[object Object]") as JSON, which is invalid. To resolve this and make your code more robust, you can implement a more flexible parsing approach. Here's a solution:

1. Create a helper function to safely parse the data:

```javascript
function safeParse(data) {
  if (typeof data === 'object') return data;
  if (typeof data !== 'string') return {};
  
  try {
    return JSON.parse(data);
  } catch (error) {
    console.warn("Failed to parse data:", error);
    return {};
  }
}
  1. Use this function in your code:
const parsedSummaryData = safeParse(session?.summary_data); props.setDetailsData( session?.dkyc_data, parsedSummaryData, // ... other props );

This approach offers several benefits:

  1. Type Safety: It handles both object and string inputs correctly.

  2. Error Handling: Parsing errors are caught and logged without crashing the application.

  3. Default Value: If parsing fails or the input is invalid, it defaults to an empty object.

  4. Simplicity: The logic is encapsulated in a reusable function.

By using this method, you'll resolve the JSON parsing error and make your code more resilient to different data formats. It also improves error handling and provides a consistent output regardless of the input format.

title: React TypeError: selectedValue.toLowerCase is not a function
body:
I'm encountering a TypeError in my React application, specifically in a component that processes some data. Here's the problematic code:

dataElements.map((ele, index) => {
  const selectedValue = ele?.selected;
  const selectedQuesMatchCheck = selectedValue.toLowerCase().includes("atch");
  const selectedQuesCorrectCheck = selectedValue.toLowerCase().includes("orrect");
  const eleQues = ele.question.toUpperCase();
  console.log("getConvertedQnaData ele = ", ele);
  // ... rest of the code
});

This code is throwing the following error:

Uncaught TypeError: selectedValue.toLowerCase is not a function

It seems that selectedValue is sometimes not a string. How can I modify this code to handle cases where selectedValue might be undefined or not a string?

The error occurs because ele.selected is not always a string, and you're trying to call toLowerCase() on it. To fix this, you need to add type checking and provide fallback values. Here's an improved version of your code:

dataElements.map((ele, index) => {
  const selectedValue = ele?.selected;
  
  // Check if selectedValue is a string before calling toLowerCase()
  const selectedValueLower = typeof selectedValue === 'string' ? selectedValue.toLowerCase() : '';

  const selectedQuesMatchCheck = selectedValueLower.includes("atch");
  const selectedQuesCorrectCheck = selectedValueLower.includes("orrect");
  
  // Use optional chaining for question as well, in case it's undefined
  const eleQues = ele?.question?.toUpperCase() || '';
  
  console.log("getConvertedQnaData ele = ", ele);

  // Return the mapped object
  return {
    selectedQuesMatchCheck,
    selectedQuesCorrectCheck,
    eleQues,
    // ... other properties you want to include
  };
});

Key changes:

  1. We create selectedValueLower which is guaranteed to be a string.

  2. We use optional chaining (?.) and provide a fallback empty string for ele.question.

  3. We use selectedValueLower for both includes() checks.

These changes ensure that:

  • toLowerCase() is only called on string values.

  • The code doesn't break if ele.selected or ele.question is undefined.

Additionally, make sure that dataElements is always an array before calling map() on it.

This solution should resolve the TypeError and make your code more robust against unexpected data structures.

title: UDP Testing Guide: Server to Mac, Server to Server
bodyMarkdown: UDP Testing Guide: Server to Mac, Server to Server
body: UDP Testing Guide: Server to Mac, Server to Server

bodyMarkdown:
This guide covers UDP testing between a server and a Mac, as well as between two servers over the internet.

## 1. Finding IP Addresses

### On Mac:

*# Wi-Fi: ipconfig getifaddr en0* 

*# Ethernet: ipconfig getifaddr en1* 

*# All interfaces: ifconfig | grep "inet " | grep -v 127.0.0.1* 

*# Public IP: curl ifconfig.me*

On Server:

*# All IPs: ip addr show* 

*# Public IP: curl ifconfig.me*

## 2. Setting Up Listeners

### On Mac or Server:

```
nc -ul 49400
```

### Alternative for Server (using Python):

```
import socket
s = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_DGRAM)
s.bind(('0.0.0.0', 49400))
print('Listening on 49400...')
while True:
    data, addr = s.recvfrom(1024)
    print(f'Received: {data} from {addr}')
```

## 3. Sending UDP Packets

### From Mac to Server:

```
echo "Test from Mac" | nc -u SERVER_IP 49400
```

### From Server to Mac:

```
echo "Test from server" | nc -u MAC_IP 49400
```

### From Server to Server:

```
echo "Test from Server A" | nc -u SERVER_B_IP 49400
```

## 4. Monitoring Network Traffic

### On Mac:

```
sudo tcpdump -i any -n udp and src SERVER_IP and port 49400
```

### On Server:

```
sudo tcpdump -i any -n udp and dst TARGET_IP and port 49400
```

## 5. Allowing Internet Traffic (Server to Server)

### Using iptables:

```
sudo iptables -A INPUT -p udp --dport 49400 -j ACCEPT
sudo iptables -A OUTPUT -p udp --sport 49400 -j ACCEPT
```

### Using firewalld:

```
sudo firewall-cmd --add-port=49400/udp --permanent
sudo firewall-cmd --reload
```

## 6. Troubleshooting

1. Check if port is in use: `ss -lun | grep :49400`

2. Verify firewall rules:

   - iptables: `sudo iptables -L INPUT -v -n | grep udp`

   - firewalld: `sudo firewall-cmd --list-all`

3. Test connectivity: `ping IP_ADDRESS`

4. Check routing: `ip route get IP_ADDRESS`

## Additional Notes

- For server-to-server communication over the internet, use public IP addresses.

- Set up port forwarding on routers for UDP port 49400 if behind NAT.

- Check cloud provider's security groups or network ACLs.

- For security, consider limiting allowed IP ranges instead of opening to all IPs.

Remember to replace `SERVER_IP`, `MAC_IP`, `SERVER_B_IP`, and `TARGET_IP` with actual IP addresses in all commands.

title: Language Ordering in LangSelectComponent
bodyMarkdown: Language Ordering in LangSelectComponent
body: Language Ordering in LangSelectComponent

Current Behavior

The LangSelectComponent currently sorts the language list using the sortLanguageList method:

sortLanguageList(languageList) {
  return languageList.slice(0, 2).concat(
    languageList.slice(2, languageList.length).sort((a, b) => {
      if (a.key < b.key) return -1;
      if (a.key > b.key) return 1;
      return 0;
    })
  );
}

This method:

  1. Keeps the first two languages in their original order.

  2. Sorts the remaining languages alphabetically by their 'key'.

The sorting is applied in the setLanguageList method:

setLanguageList(languageList) {
  // ... other code ...
  this.languageList = this.sortLanguageList(this.languageList);
}

Modifying the Order

To Maintain Original Configuration Order

  1. Option 1: Remove sorting in setLanguageList:

    setLanguageList(languageList) {
  // ... other code ...
  // Comment out or remove the following line:
  // this.languageList = this.sortLanguageList(this.languageList);
}

  2. Option 2: Modify sortLanguageList to return the original list:

    sortLanguageList(languageList) {
  return languageList;
}

    To Implement Custom Ordering

    1. Define a custom order array:
const customOrder = ['en', 'es', 'fr', 'de', 'it', /* ... */];

Modify sortLanguageList to use the custom order:

sortLanguageList(languageList) {
  return languageList.sort((a, b) => {
    return customOrder.indexOf(a.key) - customOrder.indexOf(b.key);
  });
}

Conclusion

By modifying the sortLanguageList method or its usage in setLanguageList, you can control the order of languages to suit your needs, whether maintaining the original configuration order or implementing a custom sorting logic.

title: How to manage the pion-port-range process for UDP communication?
bodyMarkdown: I'm managing a server that runs a `pion-port-range` process for UDP communication. How can I check its status, view logs, stop and start the process, and troubleshoot common issues?
body: I'm managing a server that runs a pion-port-range process for UDP communication. How can I check its status, view logs, stop and start the process, and troubleshoot common issues?

bodyMarkdown:
The `pion-port-range` process manages UDP ports (typically 49300-49500) for video communication. Here's how to manage it:

### Checking Process Status

Run:

```
ps aux | grep pion-port-range
```

You should see output like:

```
root 9463 1 0 Jun22 ? 00:00:20 ./pion-port-range-x86_64 -public-ip 117.244.99.34 -private-ip 172.28.15.79 -port 49200 -alt-port-public 49201 -minPort 49300 -maxPort 49500 -users taipvu=taipvp -tcp-port 49200
```

### Viewing Logs

Logs are typically in `/home/videokyc/pion.out`. View recent logs:

```
tail -n 100 /home/videokyc/pion.out
```

Monitor in real-time:

```
tail -f /home/videokyc/pion.out
```

### Stopping the Process

1. Find the PID:

   ```
   ps aux | grep pion-port-range
   ```

2. Stop it: 

```
sudo kill <PID>
```

If it doesn't stop, use: 

```
sudo kill -9 <PID>
```

Verify it's stopped: 

```
ps aux | grep pion-port-range
```

### Starting the Process

1. Navigate to the directory:

   ```
   cd /home/videokyc
   ```

2. Start the process: 

   ```
   sudo nohup ./pion-port-range-x86_64 -public-ip 117.244.99.34 \
   -private-ip 172.28.15.79 -port 49200 -alt-port-public 49201 \
   -minPort 49300 -maxPort 49500 -users taipvu=taipvp -tcp-port 49200 \
   > pion.out 2>&1 &
   ```

3. Verify it's running: 

   ```
   ps aux | grep pion-port-range
   ```

   ### 

   ### Troubleshooting

   1. **Process won't start**: Check logs for errors. Ensure correct permissions and IP addresses.

   2. **Communication issues**: Verify firewall settings allow UDP traffic on the specified ports.

   3. **High resource usage**: Check system resources (CPU, memory). Consider upgrading hardware if consistently high.

   4. **Unexpected stops**: Look for error messages in logs. Consider setting up as a systemd service for automatic restarts.

   ### Best Practices

   - Monitor regularly

   - Set up automated alerts for failures

   - Keep the binary updated

   - Consider implementing as a systemd service

   ### Note

   Replace IP addresses and port numbers with your actual configuration. Always use `sudo` carefully and ensure you have the necessary permissions.

title: React Component to Hide Empty Fields in Dynamic Forms
bodyMarkdown:
## Problem

In a React component that dynamically renders form fields based on a configuration and API response, empty fields were being displayed even when their corresponding values were not provided by the API. This led to a cluttered user interface with unnecessary empty fields.
body:
Problem

In a React component that dynamically renders form fields based on a configuration and API response, empty fields were being displayed even when their corresponding values were not provided by the API. This led to a cluttered user interface with unnecessary empty fields.

Solution

We modified the extraFields function in the React component to filter out empty or undefined values before rendering. Here are the key changes and their effects:

extraFields = (extraBasicText, type, half_length, parentTitle = "") => {
  // ... (existing code remains the same)

  return extraBasic.map((extraItem, i) => {
    var value = undefined;

    // ... (existing value determination logic remains the same)

    // New: Enhanced check for empty or undefined values
    if (
      (value === undefined || value === null || value === "") &&
      (!extraItem.info || extraItem.info === "")
    ) {
      return null; // Don't render this item if there's no value
    }

    // New: If the value is an array (for nested items), check if it's empty
    if (Array.isArray(value) && value.length === 0) {
      return null;
    }

    // ... (rest of the rendering logic)

  }).filter(Boolean); // New: This will remove any null items
};

Explanation of Changes

  1. Empty Value Check: We added a comprehensive check to filter out items with empty, null, or undefined values. This ensures that fields without actual data are not rendered.

  2. Array Handling: For nested items that might be arrays, we added a check to ensure empty arrays are not rendered.

  3. Null Filtering: We added .filter(Boolean) at the end of the map function to remove any null items that were returned due to the empty checks.

  4. Class Name Logic: We updated the className assignment to use utility functions for more robust empty checks:

className={
  isNotEmptyValue(value) || isNotEmptyString(extraItem.info)
    ? classnames(styles.box)
    : classnames(styles.box, styles.emptyDataParent)
}

Effects of These Changes

  1. Cleaner UI: Only fields with actual data will be displayed, reducing clutter in the user interface.

  2. Improved Performance: By not rendering empty fields, we slightly reduce the number of DOM elements, potentially improving performance for large forms.

  3. Better Data Representation: The UI now more accurately represents the actual data received from the API.

Potential Impacts on Existing Code

  1. Dependency Addition: We now rely on isNotEmptyString and isNotEmptyValue functions from kwikid-toolkit. Ensure this dependency is properly imported:
import { isNotEmptyString, isNotEmptyValue } from "kwikid-toolkit";

  1. Empty Field Behavior: Any code that previously relied on empty fields being rendered will need to be adjusted. For example, if there was any logic that counted on all configured fields being present in the DOM regardless of their values, this would need to be updated.

  2. Styling: If there were any styles applied to empty fields specifically, these may no longer be relevant and could potentially be removed.

  3. Testing: Existing tests that check for the presence of empty fields will need to be updated to expect these fields to be absent.

Conclusion

These changes provide a more user-friendly and data-accurate representation of form fields. By only rendering fields with actual data, we improve both the user experience and the performance of the component. However, it's important to thoroughly test these changes to ensure they don't negatively impact any existing functionality that may have depended on empty fields being rendered.

title: Custom Naming Configuration for Session Status
bodyMarkdown: Custom Naming Configuration for Session Status
body: Custom Naming Configuration for Session Status

There are two ways to implement the custom naming configuration, depending on your admin portal build version:

Latest Build Version

In the latest build, use this simplified configuration:

{
  "customNaming": {
    "sessions": [
      {
        "customValues": [
          {
            "updatedVal": "vpd_result_approved",
            "val": "kyc_result_approved"
          },
          {
            "updatedVal": "vpd_result_rejected",
            "val": "kyc_result_rejected"
          },
          {
            "updatedVal": "vpd_rejected",
            "val": "kyc_rejected"
          },
          {
            "updatedVal": "vpd_request_accepted",
            "val": "kyc_request_accepted"
          }
        ],
        "key": "session_status"
      }
    ]
  }
}

Old Build (VPD-Specific)

For older builds with VPD-specific implementation, use this configuration:

{
  "customNaming": {
    "sessions": [
      {
        "condition": {
          "customValues": [
            {
              "updatedVal": "vpd_result_approved",
              "val": "kyc_result_approved"
            },
            {
              "updatedVal": "vpd_result_rejected",
              "val": "kyc_result_rejected"
            },
            {
              "updatedVal": "vpd_rejected",
              "val": "kyc_rejected"
            },
            {
              "updatedVal": "vpd_request_accepted",
              "val": "kyc_request_accepted"
            }
          ],
          "key": "isVpd",
          "path": "$.extras.isVpd",
          "value": true
        },
        "key": "session_status"
      }
    ]
  }
}

Important Notes:

  1. For the latest build:

    • Simply update your admin portal to the latest version

    • Apply the configuration as shown in the first example in adminConfig

  2. For legacy builds:

    • The client must send isVpd: true in the extras field

    • This can be done either during the initial configuration or while performing sendlink

    • The configuration will only take effect when isVpd is true

Implementation Steps:

  1. Choose the appropriate configuration based on your build version

  2. Apply the configuration in your admin portal

  3. For old builds, ensure the isVpd flag is properly set

  4. Test the configuration by verifying the status values are correctly transformed

This configuration will map KYC-related status values to their VPD counterparts as specified in the customValues array.

bodyMarkdown:
Here's a step-by-step guide to set up your Pion WebRTC server as a systemd service:

1. **Create the Service File**

```
sudo nano /etc/systemd/system/pion.service
```

2. **Add the Following Configuration** Replace `/path/to/your/directory` with the actual path where your pion executable is located:

```
[Unit]
Description=Pion WebRTC Service
After=network.target

[Service]
Type=simple
User=root
WorkingDirectory=/path/to/your/directory
ExecStart=/path/to/your/directory/pion-port-range-x86_64 \
    -public-ip 117.244.99.34 \
    -private-ip 172.28.15.79 \
    -port 49200 \
    -alt-port-public 49201 \
    -minPort 49300 \
    -maxPort 49500 \
    -users taipvu=taipvp \
    -tcp-port 49200
Restart=always
RestartSec=3
StandardOutput=append:/path/to/your/directory/pion.out
StandardError=append:/path/to/your/directory/pion.out

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
```

3. **Set Proper Permissions**

```
sudo chmod 644 /etc/systemd/system/pion.service
```

4. **Enable and Start the Service**

```
# Reload systemd to recognize new service
sudo systemctl daemon-reload

# Enable service to start on boot
sudo systemctl enable pion

# Start the service
sudo systemctl start pion

# Check status
sudo systemctl status pion
```

### Common Management Commands

```
# Stop the service
sudo systemctl stop pion

# Restart the service
sudo systemctl restart pion

# View service status
sudo systemctl status pion

# View logs
sudo journalctl -u pion -f

# Disable service from starting on boot
sudo systemctl disable pion
```

### Troubleshooting

1. **If service fails to start**, check:

   - Correct paths in service file

   - File permissions

   - Log output: `sudo journalctl -u pion -f`

2. **Common Issues**:

   - CHDIR errors: Verify WorkingDirectory exists and has correct permissions

   - Permission denied: Ensure executable has correct permissions (`chmod +x`)

   - Port conflicts: Check if ports are already in use (`netstat -tulpn`)

3. **To check if ports are in use**:

```
netstat -tulpn | grep '49200\|49201'
```

### Important Notes:

- Replace `/path/to/your/directory` with the actual path where your pion executable is located

    echo "Memory Usage: $memory_usage%"
    
    if [ "$memory_usage" -gt 75 ]; then
        status="down"
        error_messages+=("Memory-usage-critical-${memory_usage}%")
        return 1
    fi
    return 0
}

# Function to check Docker containers
check_docker_containers() {
    echo "Checking Docker containers..."
    
    # Get list of exited containers with their names
    local exited_containers=$(docker ps -a --format '{{.Names}}' --filter "status=exited")
    
    # Get list of containers with non-healthy status (if they have health checks)
    local unhealthy_containers=$(docker ps -a --format '{{.Names}}' --filter "health=unhealthy")
    
    local docker_errors=()

    # Check exited containers
    if [ ! -z "$exited_containers" ]; then
        while IFS= read -r container; do
            echo "Container Exited: $container"
            docker_errors+=("$container(exited)")
        done <<< "$exited_containers"
    fi

    # Check unhealthy containers
    if [ ! -z "$unhealthy_containers" ]; then
        while IFS= read -r container; do
            echo "Container Unhealthy: $container"
            docker_errors+=("$container(unhealthy)")
        done <<< "$unhealthy_containers"
    fi

    # If any docker containers are down or unhealthy, add them to error messages
    if [ ${#docker_errors[@]} -gt 0 ]; then
        status="down"
        error_messages+=("Docker-issues-(${docker_errors[*]})")
        return 1
    else
        echo "All Docker containers are running properly"
    fi
    return 0
}

# Function to combine error messages
combine_error_messages() {
    if [ ${#error_messages[@]} -eq 0 ]; then
        msg="OK"
    else
        # Join array elements with '|' as separator
        msg=$(IFS='|'; echo "${error_messages[*]}")
    fi
}

# Main monitoring logic
echo "=== Starting System Monitoring ==="
echo "Time: $(date)"
echo "------------------------"

# Run all checks
check_disk_space
check_memory_usage
check_docker_containers

# Combine all error messages
combine_error_messages

echo "Final Message: $msg"

# Log the results (optional)
echo "$(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S') - Status: $status - Message: $msg" >> /var/log/system_monitor.log

bodyMarkdown:
## Overview

This guide demonstrates how to set up a file transfer system between two servers where one server (App Server) has no direct internet access but can connect to another server (Web Server) via HTTPS (port 443).

## Architecture

```
Internet <---> Web Server (172.28.15.79:443) <---> App Server
```

## Prerequisites

- Web Server with:

  - Internet access

  - Nginx installed

  - SSL certificates configured

- App Server with:

  - No direct internet access

  - Access to Web Server on port 443

## Setup Instructions

### 1. Web Server Configuration

## 1.1 Create Directory Structure

```
# Create base directory for files
mkdir -p /usr/share/nginx/html/packages/{python,software,scripts,tools}

# Set proper permissions
chmod 755 /usr/share/nginx/html/packages
chown -R nginx:nginx /usr/share/nginx/html/packages
```

## 1.2 Configure Nginx

Edit `/etc/nginx/nginx.conf`:

```
http {
    # ... (existing configurations)

    server {
        listen       443 ssl;
        server_name  _;
        
        # SSL Configuration
        ssl_certificate /path/to/your/certificate.cer;
        ssl_certificate_key /path/to/your/private.key;
        ssl_protocols TLSv1.2 TLSv1.3;

        # Proxy configuration (if needed)
        location / {
            proxy_pass http://your-backend-server:port;
        }

        # File serving location
        location /packages/ {
            root   /usr/share/nginx/html;
            autoindex on;
            allow all;
            add_header Content-Type application/octet-stream;
        }
    }
}
```

## 1.3 Test and Reload Nginx

```
nginx -t
systemctl reload nginx
```

### 2. Using the File Server

## 2.1 For Python Packages

On Web Server:

```
# Navigate to python packages directory
cd /usr/share/nginx/html/packages/python

# Download or copy Python packages here
yumdownloader --destdir=. python3-pip python3-setuptools
```

## 2.2 For General Software/Files

```
# Copy any files to appropriate directories
cp your-software.tar.gz /usr/share/nginx/html/packages/software/
cp your-script.sh /usr/share/nginx/html/packages/scripts/
```

### 3. Accessing Files from App Server

## 3.1 Download Files Using curl

```
# Create directory for downloads
mkdir -p /tmp/downloads
cd /tmp/downloads

# Download files using curl
curl -k https://172.28.15.79:443/packages/python/your-package.rpm -O
curl -k https://172.28.15.79:443/packages/software/your-software.tar.gz -O
```

## 3.2 Basic Script for File Download

Create `/usr/local/bin/get-file.sh`:

```
#!/bin/bash

# Configuration
WEBSERVER="172.28.15.79:443"
DOWNLOAD_DIR="/tmp/downloads"

# Usage function
usage() {
    echo "Usage: $0 <category> <filename>"
    echo "Categories: python, software, scripts, tools"
    echo "Example: $0 python python3-pip.rpm"
    exit 1
}

# Check arguments
if [ $# -lt 2 ]; then
    usage
fi

CATEGORY=$1
FILENAME=$2

# Create download directory
mkdir -p "$DOWNLOAD_DIR"
cd "$DOWNLOAD_DIR"

# Download file
echo "Downloading $FILENAME from $CATEGORY..."
curl -k "https://${WEBSERVER}/packages/${CATEGORY}/${FILENAME}" -O

if [ $? -eq 0 ]; then
    echo "Successfully downloaded to ${DOWNLOAD_DIR}/${FILENAME}"
else
    echo "Download failed!"
fi
```

Make it executable:

```
chmod +x /usr/local/bin/get-file.sh
```

## Usage Examples

### 1. Python Packages

```
# Download Python package
get-file.sh python python3-pip-9.0.3-13.el8.noarch.tgz

# Install package
cd /
tar xzf /tmp/downloads/python3-pip-9.0.3-13.el8.noarch.tgz
```

### 2. Software Installation Files

```
# Download software
get-file.sh software mysql-server.rpm

# Download scripts
get-file.sh scripts backup.sh
```

## Directory Structure

```
/usr/share/nginx/html/packages/
├── python/           # Python packages
├── software/         # Installation files
├── scripts/          # Shell scripts
└── tools/            # Utilities and tools
```

## Best Practices

1. Organize files into appropriate directories

2. Maintain consistent naming conventions

3. Regular cleanup of old/unused files

4. Monitor disk space usage

5. Keep an inventory of available files

## Security Considerations

1. Use HTTPS with valid certificates

2. Implement access control if needed

3. Regular security audits

4. Monitor access logsTroubleshooting

   1. Check Nginx logs:

   ```
   tail -f /var/log/nginx/error.log
   tail -f /var/log/nginx/access.log
   ```

   2. Test connectivity:

   ```
   # On App Server
   telnet 172.28.15.79 443
   curl -v -k https://172.28.15.79/packages/
   ```

   3. Check file permissions:

   ```
   ls -l /usr/share/nginx/html/packages/
   ```

There you go!

title: Config | Agent Portal | Hide empty keys in extras if value is not present
bodyMarkdown: Config | Agent Portal | Hide empty keys in extras if value is not present
body: Config | Agent Portal | Hide empty keys in extras if value is not present

In the Agent Portal configuration, you can hide keys from the extras object when their corresponding values are empty using the `isHideEmptyExtraValues` flag.

You can use the `isHideEmptyExtraValues` configuration flag to hide keys with empty values:

{
    "isHideEmptyExtraValues": true
}

Consider this JSON data structure where some bank entries have empty values:

{
    "banks": [
        {
            "bank_name": "Axis",
            "account_type": "Savings"
        },
        {
            "bank_name": "",
            "account_type": ""
        },
        {
            "bank_name": "",
            "account_type": ""
        },
        {
            "bank_name": "Kotak",
            "account_type": "Savings"
        }
    ]
}

When isHideEmptyExtraValues is set to true, the empty entries will be hidden from the output.

{
    "banks": [
        {
            "bank_name": "Axis",
            "account_type": "Savings"
        },
        {
            "bank_name": "Kotak",
            "account_type": "Savings"
        }
    ]
}

Make sure to use latest version should be deployed.

body: Working with Amazon ECR (Elastic Container Registry)

bodyMarkdown:
**1.Prerequisites**

- AWS CLI must be installed

- AWS credentials must be configured (`aws configure`)

- Docker must be installed on your server

**2. Authentication**

```
aws ecr get-login-password --region ap-south-1 | docker login --username AWS --password-stdin 740186269845.dkr.ecr.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com
```

This command:

1. Generates an authentication token for ECR

2. Logs into Docker using AWS credentials

3. Valid for 12 hours

**3. Pulling Images**

```
docker pull 740186269845.dkr.ecr.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/vkyc-signalling-server:auatv2
```

Where:

- `740186269845.dkr.ecr.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com` is your ECR registry URI

- `vkyc-signalling-server` is your repository name

- `auatv2` is your image tag

**4. Running Containers**

```
docker run [options] 740186269845.dkr.ecr.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/vkyc-signalling-server:auatv2

body: Troubleshooting 502 Bad Gateway Error in Face Match Custom API

bodyMarkdown:
**Server 1 - Fino Facematch Server**

**Problem:** Receiving 502 Bad Gateway errors when making POST requests to `/ml/face_match_custom` endpoint, while `/kms/access-token` requests succeed.

**Error Logs:**

```
ml.getkwikid.com--/ml/face_match_custom --- HTTP/1.1" 502 150
Service status: failed (Result: exit-code) status=255
```

**Investigation Steps:**

1. Checked NGINX logs:

```
tail -f /var/log/nginx/access.log
tail -f /var/log/nginx/error.log
```

2. Verified network connectivity:

```
ping 10.71.89.82  # Successful
ping 10.71.87.17  # Successful
```

**Server 2 - AUAT Server**

```
systemctl list-units --type=service --all
```

```
Location: /etc/systemd/system/facematch_attendance_backend.service
Status: failed (Result: exit-code)
Port: 3360
```

**Resolution Steps:**

1. Found service failure on AUAT server

2. Checked logs in `/home/ubuntu/facematch_attendance_backend/`

3. Restarted service:

```
sudo systemctl restart facematch_attendance_backend.service
```

Note Fino facematch is legacy API. (OLD)

body: Python script to perform VLOOKUP-like operation between two CSVs with multiple matches

bodyMarkdown:
This script performs a VLOOKUP-like operation between two CSV files, handling cases
where there might be multiple matches. It's particularly useful when you have:

- A primary CSV with unique identifiers
- A secondary CSV with multiple entries per identifier

Requirements:

- pandas
- Python 3.x

```
import pandas as pd

def perform_csv_lookup(csv1_path: str, csv2_path: str) -> None:
    """
    Performs lookup operation between two CSVs and handles multiple matches.
    
    Args:
        csv1_path (str): Path to first CSV containing unique identifiers
        csv2_path (str): Path to second CSV containing multiple entries
    
    Example:
        csv1 (users.csv):
        id,name
        FINO-000000680592,John
        
        csv2 (data.csv):
        id,transaction,amount
        FINO-000000680592,buy,100
        FINO-000000680592,sell,200
    """
    # Read CSVs
    df1 = pd.read_csv(csv1_path)
    df2 = pd.read_csv(csv2_path)
    
    # Display column names
    print("CSV 1 columns:", df1.columns.tolist())
    print("CSV 2 columns:", df2.columns.tolist())
    
    # Get column names for lookup
    lookup_col1 = input("Enter column name from first CSV containing IDs: ")
    lookup_col2 = input("Enter column name from second CSV containing IDs: ")
    
    # Clean IDs - remove whitespace and convert to string
    df1[lookup_col1] = df1[lookup_col1].astype(str).str.strip()
    df2[lookup_col2] = df2[lookup_col2].astype(str).str.strip()
    
    # Perform merge (VLOOKUP equivalent)
    result = pd.merge(
        df1,
        df2,
        left_on=lookup_col1,
        right_on=lookup_col2,
        how='left'  # Keeps all records from first CSV
    )
    
    # Save results
    result.to_csv('mapped_results.csv', index=False)
    
    # Display statistics
    print(f"\nResults:")
    print(f"Records in first CSV: {len(df1)}")
    print(f"Records in second CSV: {len(df2)}")
    print(f"Matched records: {len(result)}")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    csv1_path = "users.csv"    # CSV with unique identifiers
    csv2_path = "data.csv"     # CSV with multiple entries
    perform_csv_lookup(csv1_path, csv2_path)
```

title: CBI RRB | Nginx SSL Certificate Chain Verification Error with DigiCert Certificate
bodyMarkdown: CBI RRB | Nginx SSL Certificate Chain Verification Error with DigiCert Certificate
body: CBI RRB | Nginx SSL Certificate Chain Verification Error with DigiCert Certificate

bodyMarkdown:
**Environment:**

- Web Server: Nginx

- SSL Certificate Provider: DigiCert

- Certificate Type: Wildcard (\*.rrbcbi.co.in)

- Issuer: GeoTrust TLS RSA CA G1

## Current Configuration

```
ssl_certificate /root/ssl/star_rrbcbi_co_in.cer;
ssl_certificate_key /root/ssl/rrbserver.key;
ssl_protocols TLSv1.2 TLSv1.3;
```

## Root Cause

The intermediate certificate from DigiCert is missing in the certificate chain. The browser needs the complete chain to verify the certificate's authenticity:

- Your Domain Certificate (\*.rrbcbi.co.in)

- Intermediate Certificate (GeoTrust TLS RSA CA G1)

- Root Certificate (already present in browsers)

## Solution

1. **Create a backup of your current certificate:**

```
cp /root/ssl/star_rrbcbi_co_in.cer /root/ssl/star_rrbcbi_co_in.cer.backup
```

2. **Create a full chain certificate:**

```
# Create a new file for the full chain
cat /root/ssl/star_rrbcbi_co_in.cer > /root/ssl/fullchain.cer
# Append the intermediate certificate
cat /root/ssl/intermediate.cer >> /root/ssl/fullchain.cer
```

3. **Update Nginx configuration:**

```
# SSL Configuration
ssl_certificate /root/ssl/fullchain.cer;
ssl_certificate_key /root/ssl/rrbserver.key;

# Recommended SSL Settings
ssl_session_timeout 1d;
ssl_session_cache shared:SSL:50m;
ssl_session_tickets off;

ssl_protocols TLSv1.2 TLSv1.3;
ssl_ciphers ECDHE-ECDSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256:ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256:ECDHE-ECDSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384:ECDHE-RSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384:ECDHE-ECDSA-CHACHA20-POLY1305:ECDHE-RSA-CHACHA20-POLY1305:DHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256:DHE-RSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384;
ssl_prefer_server_ciphers off;
```

4. **Test configuration and reload Nginx:**

```
nginx -t
nginx -s reload
```

5. **Verify the certificate chain:**

```
openssl s_client -connect localhost:443
```

## Additional Security Recommendations

Add these optional security headers:

```
# HSTS (uncomment if you're sure about HTTPS-only)
# add_header Strict-Transport-Security "max-age=63072000" always;

# Other security headers
add_header X-Frame-Options SAMEORIGIN;
add_header X-Content-Type-Options nosniff;
add_header X-XSS-Protection "1; mode=block";
```

## Troubleshooting Steps

1. **Verify certificate information:**

```
openssl x509 -in /root/ssl/star_rrbcbi_co_in.cer -text -noout
```

2. **Check certificate chain:**

```
openssl verify -CAfile /root/ssl/intermediate.cer /root/ssl/star_rrbcbi_co_in.cer
```

3. **Test SSL connection:**

```
openssl s_client -connect localhost:443 -servername rrbcbi.co.in
```

## Common Issues

1. **Wrong Certificate Order:**

   - Domain certificate must come first

   - Intermediate certificate must come second

2. **File Permissions:**

```
chmod 644 /root/ssl/fullchain.cer
chmod 600 /root/ssl/rrbserver.key
```

3. **DNS Resolution Issues:** Test with:

```
ping rrbcbi.co.in
dig rrbcbi.co.in
```

## Useful Resources

- [DigiCert Documentation](https://docs.digicert.com/)

- [Nginx SSL Configuration](https://nginx.org/en/docs/http/configuring_https_servers.html)

- [SSL Labs Server Test](https://www.ssllabs.com/ssltest/)

#!/bin/bash

# Uptime Kuma's unique URL for your monitor
KUMA_URL="https://monitor.test.getkwikid.com/api/push/<new_key_from_kuma>"

# Initialize status and message array
status="up"
declare -a error_messages=()

# Function to check disk space
check_disk_space() {
    local disk_space=$(df -h / | awk 'NR==2 {print $5}' | sed 's/%//')
    echo "Disk Usage: $disk_space%"
    
    if [ "$disk_space" -gt 80 ]; then
        status="down"
        error_messages+=("Disk-space-critical-${disk_space}%")
        return 1
    fi
    return 0
}

# Function to check memory usage
check_memory_usage() {
    local memory_usage=$(free | awk '/Mem/{printf("%.0f", $3/$2 * 100.0)}')
    echo "Memory Usage: $memory_usage%"
    
    if [ "$memory_usage" -gt 75 ]; then
        status="down"
        error_messages+=("Memory-usage-critical-${memory_usage}%")
        return 1
    fi
    return 0
}

# Function to check Docker containers
check_docker_containers() {
    echo "Checking Docker containers..."
    
    # Get list of exited containers with their names
    local exited_containers=$(docker ps -a --format '{{.Names}}' --filter "status=exited")

    # Get list of containers with non-healthy status (if they have health checks)
    local unhealthy_containers=$(docker ps -a --format '{{.Names}}' --filter "health=unhealthy")

    local docker_errors=()

    # Check exited containers
    if [ ! -z "$exited_containers" ]; then
        while IFS= read -r container; do
            echo "Container Exited: $container"
            docker_errors+=("$container(exited)")
        done <<< "$exited_containers"
    fi

    # Check unhealthy containers
    if [ ! -z "$unhealthy_containers" ]; then
        while IFS= read -r container; do
            echo "Container Unhealthy: $container"
            docker_errors+=("$container(unhealthy)")
        done <<< "$unhealthy_containers"
    fi

    # If any docker containers are down or unhealthy, add them to error messages
    if [ ${#docker_errors[@]} -gt 0 ]; then
        status="down"
        error_messages+=("Docker-issues-(${docker_errors[*]})")
        return 1
    else
        echo "All Docker containers are running properly"
    fi
    return 0
}

# Function to combine error messages
combine_error_messages() {
    if [ ${#error_messages[@]} -eq 0 ]; then
        msg="OK"
    else
        # Join array elements with '|' as separator
        msg=$(IFS='|'; echo "${error_messages[*]}")
    fi
}

# Main monitoring logic
echo "=== Starting System Monitoring ==="
echo "Time: $(date)"
echo "------------------------"

# Run all checks
check_disk_space
check_memory_usage
check_docker_containers

# Combine all error messages
combine_error_messages

echo "------------------------"
echo "Final Status: $status"
echo "Final Message: $msg"

# Push the status and message to Uptime Kuma
curl -X GET "$KUMA_URL?status=$status&msg=$msg"

# Log the results (optional)
echo "$(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S') - Status: $status - Message: $msg" >> /var/log/system_monitor.log
```

bodyMarkdown:
I encountered a 500 Internal Server Error when calling the PAN verification API endpoint:

```
https://vkycuat.unitybank.co.in:3357/v1/verify_pan/83472473c3
```

## Initial Troubleshooting Steps

1. First, check if any existing Docker containers or systemctl services are running for the backend API by checking the nginx routing.

2. Verify the service associated with the endpoint - in this case, `verify_pan` is handled by `kwikid_poc_ipv.service`.

3. To check for non-running services, use:

```
systemctl list-units --type=service --all
```

4. Check service logs:

```
tail -f /home/ubuntu/Kwikid_ipv_poc/kwikid_ipv_backend_new/ipv_logs
tail -f /home/ubuntu/Kwikid_ipv_poc/kwikid_ipv_backend_new/error_logs
```

5. For Gunicorn processes:

```
ps aux | grep gunicorn
```

## Understanding HTTP Status Codes

- 500: Internal server error (code issue)

- 502: Service not running or port not listening

- 404: Endpoint doesn't exist or incorrect endpoint

## Solution Process

1. Imported the API cURL into Postman for easier testing instead of going through the complete journey each time:

```
curl --location 'https://vkycuat.unitybank.co.in:3357/v1/verify_pan/83472473c3' \
--header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
[other headers...]
--data '{"pan_card_number":"DWUPM5956A","name":"AFRID ABDUL SATTAR MULLA","dob":"31/07/1998","dedupe":0}'
```

2. The initial error was traced to:

```
/app/event_task_binding/api/bindtask.py", line 99, in bind_synchronous_tasks
```

3. Checked logs in Docker containers:

- kwikid-event-handler-setup_event-task-binding_1

- kwikid-event-handler-setup_notification-service_1

- kwikid-event-handler-setup_fluentd_1

4. Found that the preops API for pan-signature wasn't accessible.

5. Located the nginx configuration at `/etc/nginx/sites-enabled/kwikid_poc_ipv`:

```
location /api/auth/pan-signature {
    proxy_pass http://localhost:7091/api/auth/pan-signature;
    proxy_pass_request_headers on;
}
```

6. Final issue was permissions on the JKS file. Fixed with:

```
sudo chown www-data:www-data pan_key.jks
sudo chmod 664 pan_key.jks
```

## Key Learning

While the final solution was a simple permissions issue, the debugging process required systematically checking multiple components: service status, logs, Docker containers, nginx configuration, and file permissions.

Remember to check file permissions early in the debugging process when dealing with certificate or key files, as it can save considerable troubleshooting time.

title: How to analyze Nginx logs by session ID or user ID?

body: How to analyze Nginx logs by session ID or user ID ?

bodyMarkdown:
This guide demonstrates how to create and use a Bash script to analyze Nginx logs, filtering by session ID or user ID. The script provides a detailed analysis of log entries including request timelines, status code distribution, and HTTP methods used.

## Prerequisites

- Access to Nginx log files (typically in `/var/log/nginx/`)

- Root access or appropriate permissions

- Basic knowledge of Bash scripting

## Server Information

The script can be used on your application servers. Example paths:

```
unity.prod.vkyc.app1.165 
unity.prod.vkyc.app2.73
```

## Quick Usage

If the script is already created, you can run it directly:

```
./analyze_nginx_logs_single.sh -f /var/log/nginx/access.log -s 40a424ef-b954-40c6-b656-07fbeab83559 -u 8143580019
```

Example:

```
./analyze_nginx_logs_single.sh -f /var/log/nginx/access.log -s 40a424ef-b954-40c6-b656-07fbeab83559 -u 8143580019
```

## Creating the Script

1. Create a new file:

```
vi analyze_nginx_logs_single.sh
```

2. Copy and paste the following script:

```
#!/bin/bash

# Help function
show_help() {

bodyMarkdown:
This is the script which you can add wherever the kwikid_ipv_backend_new is present.

```
import csv
from datetime import datetime
import re
from collections import defaultdict

def parse_log_line(line):
    """Parse a single log line and extract relevant information."""
    # Regular expression for parsing log lines with different formats
    log_patterns = [
        # For error_logs format
        r'\[(\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2} \d{2}:\d{2}:\d{2} [+-]\d{4})\] \[(\d+)\] \[(\w+)\] (.*)',
        # For ipv_logs format
        r'.*\[(\d{2}/\w+/\d{4}:\d{2}:\d{2}:\d{2} [+-]\d{4})\] "(.*?)" (\d{3}) (\d+) "(.*?)" "(.*?)"'
    ]
    
    for pattern in log_patterns:
        match = re.match(pattern, line)
        if match:
            if len(match.groups()) == 4:  # error_logs format
                timestamp_str, pid, level, message = match.groups()
                try:
                    timestamp = datetime.strptime(timestamp_str, '%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S %z')
                except ValueError:
                    timestamp = None
                return {
                    'type': 'error_log',
                    'timestamp': timestamp,
                    'pid': pid,
                    'level': level,
                    'message': message.strip()
                }
            else:  # ipv_logs format
                timestamp_str, request, status, size, referer, user_agent = match.groups()
                try:
                    timestamp = datetime.strptime(timestamp_str, '%d/%b/%Y:%H:%M:%S %z')
                except ValueError:
                    timestamp = None
                return {
                    'type': 'ipv_log',
                    'timestamp': timestamp,
                    'request': request,
                    'status': status,
                    'size': size,
                    'referer': referer,
                    'user_agent': user_agent
                }
    return None

def analyze_request(request):
    """Analyze the HTTP request string to extract method and endpoint."""
    parts = request.split()
    if len(parts) >= 2:
        return {
            'method': parts[0],
            'endpoint': parts[1]
        }
    return None

def analyze_session_logs(log_content, session_id):
    """Analyze logs for a specific session ID."""
    session_timeline = []
    api_stats = defaultdict(lambda: {'count': 0, 'methods': defaultdict(int)})
    file_operations = []
    endpoints = defaultdict(int)
    
    for line in log_content.split('\n'):
        if not line.strip() or session_id not in line:
            continue
            
        parsed = parse_log_line(line)
        if not parsed:
            continue

        # Add to timeline
        if parsed['type'] == 'error_log':
            session_timeline.append({
                'timestamp': parsed['timestamp'],
                'type': 'system',
                'action': parsed['message'],
                'level': parsed['level']
            })
            
            # Track API endpoints from error logs
            if 'GET' in parsed['message'] or 'POST' in parsed['message'] or 'OPTIONS' in parsed['message']:
                parts = parsed['message'].split()
                if len(parts) >= 2:
                    method = parts[0]
                    endpoint = parts[1]
                    api_stats[endpoint]['count'] += 1
                    api_stats[endpoint]['methods'][method] += 1
                    
                    # Track file operations
                    if 'upload_part' in endpoint or 'download_content' in endpoint:
                        file_operations.append({
                            'timestamp': parsed['timestamp'],
                            'operation': parsed['message']
                        })
        
        elif parsed['type'] == 'ipv_log':
            request_info = analyze_request(parsed['request'])
            if request_info:
                session_timeline.append({
                    'timestamp': parsed['timestamp'],
                    'type': 'http',
                    'method': request_info['method'],
                    'endpoint': request_info['endpoint'],
                    'status': parsed['status']
                })
                
                api_stats[request_info['endpoint']]['count'] += 1
                api_stats[request_info['endpoint']]['methods'][request_info['method']] += 1
                endpoints[request_info['endpoint']] += 1

    return {
        'timeline': sorted(session_timeline, key=lambda x: x['timestamp'] if x['timestamp'] else datetime.min),
        'api_stats': api_stats,
        'file_operations': sorted(file_operations, key=lambda x: x['timestamp'] if x['timestamp'] else datetime.min),
        'endpoints': endpoints
    }

def write_session_timeline_csv(timeline, filename='session_timeline.csv'):
    """Write session timeline to CSV file."""
    with open(filename, 'w', newline='') as f:
        writer = csv.writer(f)
        writer.writerow(['Timestamp', 'Type', 'Action/Method', 'Endpoint/Message', 'Status/Level'])
        
        for entry in timeline:
            timestamp = entry['timestamp'].strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S') if entry['timestamp'] else ''
            if entry['type'] == 'http':
                writer.writerow([
                    timestamp,
                    entry['type'],
                    entry['method'],
                    entry['endpoint'],
                    entry['status']
                ])
            else:
                writer.writerow([
                    timestamp,
                    entry['type'],
                    '',
                    entry['action'],
                    entry.get('level', '')
                ])

def write_api_stats_csv(api_stats, filename='session_api_stats.csv'):
    """Write API statistics to CSV file."""
    with open(filename, 'w', newline='') as f:
        writer = csv.writer(f)
        writer.writerow(['Endpoint', 'Total Count', 'GET', 'POST', 'OPTIONS'])
        
        for endpoint, stats in api_stats.items():
            row = [
                endpoint,
                stats['count'],
                stats['methods'].get('GET', 0),
                stats['methods'].get('POST', 0),
                stats['methods'].get('OPTIONS', 0)
            ]
            writer.writerow(row)

def write_file_operations_csv(file_operations, filename='session_file_operations.csv'):
    """Write file operations to CSV file."""
    with open(filename, 'w', newline='') as f:
        writer = csv.writer(f)
        writer.writerow(['Timestamp', 'Operation'])
        
        for op in file_operations:
            writer.writerow([
                op['timestamp'].strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S') if op['timestamp'] else '',
                op['operation']
            ])

def main():
    # Specific session ID to analyze
    session_id = "f6306833-f141-455d-9e4b-b03aac8c7dd1"
    
    # Read and combine both log files
    log_content = ""
    try:
        with open('error_logs', 'r') as f:
            log_content += f.read() + "\n"
    except FileNotFoundError:
        print("Warning: error_logs file not found")
    
    try:
        with open('ipv_logs', 'r') as f:
            log_content += f.read()
    except FileNotFoundError:
        print("Warning: ipv_logs file not found")

    # Analyze logs
    analysis = analyze_session_logs(log_content, session_id)

    # Generate CSV reports
    write_session_timeline_csv(analysis['timeline'])
    write_api_stats_csv(analysis['api_stats'])
    write_file_operations_csv(analysis['file_operations'])

    # Print summary

This is the script which you can add wherever the kwikid_ipv_backend_new is present.

import csv
from datetime import datetime
import re
from collections import defaultdict

def parse_log_line(line):
    """Parse a single log line and extract relevant information."""
    # Regular expression for parsing log lines with different formats
    log_patterns = [
        # For error_logs format
        r'\[(\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2} \d{2}:\d{2}:\d{2} [+-]\d{4})\] \[(\d+)\] \[(\w+)\] (.*)',
        # For ipv_logs format
        r'.*\[(\d{2}/\w+/\d{4}:\d{2}:\d{2}:\d{2} [+-]\d{4})\] "(.*?)" (\d{3}) (\d+) "(.*?)" "(.*?)"'
    ]
    
    for pattern in log_patterns:
        match = re.match(pattern, line)
        if match:
            if len(match.groups()) == 4:  # error_logs format
                timestamp_str, pid, level, message = match.groups()
                try:
                    timestamp = datetime.strptime(timestamp_str, '%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S %z')
                except ValueError:
                    timestamp = None
                return {
                    'type': 'error_log',
                    'timestamp': timestamp,
                    'pid': pid,
                    'level': level,
                    'message': message.strip()
                }
            else:  # ipv_logs format
                timestamp_str, request, status, size, referer, user_agent = match.groups()
                try:
                    timestamp = datetime.strptime(timestamp_str, '%d/%b/%Y:%H:%M:%S %z')
                except ValueError:
                    timestamp = None
                return {
                    'type': 'ipv_log',
                    'timestamp': timestamp,
                    'request': request,
                    'status': status,
                    'size': size,
                    'referer': referer,
                    'user_agent': user_agent
                }
    return None

def analyze_request(request):
    """Analyze the HTTP request string to extract method and endpoint."""
    parts = request.split()
    if len(parts) >= 2:
        return {
            'method': parts[0],
            'endpoint': parts[1]
        }
    return None

def analyze_session_logs(log_content, session_id):
    """Analyze logs for a specific session ID."""
    session_timeline = []
    api_stats = defaultdict(lambda: {'count': 0, 'methods': defaultdict(int)})
    file_operations = []
    endpoints = defaultdict(int)
    
    for line in log_content.split('\n'):
        if not line.strip() or session_id not in line:
            continue
            
        parsed = parse_log_line(line)
        if not parsed:
            continue

        # Add to timeline
        if parsed['type'] == 'error_log':
            session_timeline.append({
                'timestamp': parsed['timestamp'],
                'type': 'system',
                'action': parsed['message'],
                'level': parsed['level']
            })
            
            # Track API endpoints from error logs
            if 'GET' in parsed['message'] or 'POST' in parsed['message'] or 'OPTIONS' in parsed['message']:
                parts = parsed['message'].split()
                if len(parts) >= 2:
                    method = parts[0]
                    endpoint = parts[1]
                    api_stats[endpoint]['count'] += 1
                    api_stats[endpoint]['methods'][method] += 1
                    
                    # Track file operations
                    if 'upload_part' in endpoint or 'download_content' in endpoint:
                        file_operations.append({
                            'timestamp': parsed['timestamp'],
                            'operation': parsed['message']
                        })
        
        elif parsed['type'] == 'ipv_log':
            request_info = analyze_request(parsed['request'])
            if request_info:
                session_timeline.append({
                    'timestamp': parsed['timestamp'],
                    'type': 'http',
                    'method': request_info['method'],
                    'endpoint': request_info['endpoint'],
                    'status': parsed['status']
                })
                
                api_stats[request_info['endpoint']]['count'] += 1
                api_stats[request_info['endpoint']]['methods'][request_info['method']] += 1
                endpoints[request_info['endpoint']] += 1

    return {
        'timeline': sorted(session_timeline, key=lambda x: x['timestamp'] if x['timestamp'] else datetime.min),
        'api_stats': api_stats,
        'file_operations': sorted(file_operations, key=lambda x: x['timestamp'] if x['timestamp'] else datetime.min),
        'endpoints': endpoints
    }

def write_session_timeline_csv(timeline, filename='session_timeline.csv'):
    """Write session timeline to CSV file."""
    with open(filename, 'w', newline='') as f:
        writer = csv.writer(f)
        writer.writerow(['Timestamp', 'Type', 'Action/Method', 'Endpoint/Message', 'Status/Level'])
        
        for entry in timeline:
            timestamp = entry['timestamp'].strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S') if entry['timestamp'] else ''
            if entry['type'] == 'http':
                writer.writerow([
                    timestamp,
                    entry['type'],
                    entry['method'],
                    entry['endpoint'],
                    entry['status']
                ])
            else:
                writer.writerow([
                    timestamp,
                    entry['type'],
                    '',
                    entry['action'],
                    entry.get('level', '')
                ])

def write_api_stats_csv(api_stats, filename='session_api_stats.csv'):
    """Write API statistics to CSV file."""
    with open(filename, 'w', newline='') as f:
        writer = csv.writer(f)
        writer.writerow(['Endpoint', 'Total Count', 'GET', 'POST', 'OPTIONS'])
        
        for endpoint, stats in api_stats.items():
            row = [
                endpoint,
                stats['count'],
                stats['methods'].get('GET', 0),
                stats['methods'].get('POST', 0),
                stats['methods'].get('OPTIONS', 0)
            ]
            writer.writerow(row)

def write_file_operations_csv(file_operations, filename='session_file_operations.csv'):
    """Write file operations to CSV file."""
    with open(filename, 'w', newline='') as f:
        writer = csv.writer(f)
        writer.writerow(['Timestamp', 'Operation'])
        
        for op in file_operations:
            writer.writerow([
                op['timestamp'].strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S') if op['timestamp'] else '',
                op['operation']
            ])

def main():
    # Specific session ID to analyze
    session_id = "f6306833-f141-455d-9e4b-b03aac8c7dd1"
    
    # Read and combine both log files
    log_content = ""
    try:
        with open('error_logs', 'r') as f:
            log_content += f.read() + "\n"
    except FileNotFoundError:
        print("Warning: error_logs file not found")
    
    try:
        with open('ipv_logs', 'r') as f:
            log_content += f.read()
    except FileNotFoundError:
        print("Warning: ipv_logs file not found")

    # Analyze logs
    analysis = analyze_session_logs(log_content, session_id)

    # Generate CSV reports
    write_session_timeline_csv(analysis['timeline'])
    write_api_stats_csv(analysis['api_stats'])
    write_file_operations_csv(analysis['file_operations'])

    # Print summary
    print(f"\nAnalysis complete for session: {session_id}")
    print("\nGenerated files:")
    print("1. session_timeline.csv - Chronological timeline of all session events")
    print("2. session_api_stats.csv - API endpoint usage statistics")
    print("3. session_file_operations.csv - File upload/download operations")
    
    print("\nEndpoint Summary:")
    for endpoint, count in sorted(analysis['endpoints'].items(), key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True):
        print(f"{count:4d} calls to {endpoint}")

    print(f"\nTotal Events: {len(analysis['timeline'])}")
    print(f"Total File Operations: {len(analysis['file_operations'])}")
    print(f"Total Unique Endpoints: {len(analysis['endpoints'])}")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

title: TATA | Clear Server Space
bodyMarkdown: How to clear the server space?
body: How to clear the server space?

bodyMarkdown:
To clear space, first empty the dir `video_parts` from celery container. To further clear space clear logs & if still needed restart all the docker containers. Do Not restart the DB (database) container's (eg. scylla)

1. `docker exec -it <celery_container> bash`

   a. Replace `<celery_container>` with the celery's docker container id/name and run the command.

   b. Run `cd /home/ubuntu/Kwikid_ipv_poc/kwikid_ipv_backend_new/video_part/`

   c. Run `ls` , Run `rm -rf ./*`

2. To truncate all logs: Run `sudo find /var/log -type f -name "*.log" -exec truncate -s 0 {} +`

3. To truncate all docker logs: Run `sudo find /var/lib/docker/containers/*/ -type f -name "*-json.log" -exec truncate -s 0 {} +`

4. To restart all docker containers: run `docker restart <container_id_or_name>`, replace the `<container_id_or_name>` with the actual container's id or name.

bodyMarkdown:
Use `Refresh` Button on Admin / Auditor Portal to reinitiate the video merge process. Few mins later come back, (By closing the previous Session Details on Admin Portal / Skip the selected session on Auditor Portal) to check, if the video is fully playable or not.

---

- To Confirm the blob at that timestamp is corrupted:

  - Open Network Tab on Inspect Tool (Ctrl+Shft+I), Select all, & filter for `agent_video_screen`, get the url. [![enter image description here](https://stackoverflowteams.com/c/kwikid/images/s/fc366204-c960-42b9-9c9d-67de7b004a55.png)](https://stackoverflowteams.com/c/kwikid/images/s/fc366204-c960-42b9-9c9d-67de7b004a55.png)
  - Download the video by pasting the copied URL on new tab and pressing Enter.
  - Play the video on device's media player and confirm that the video is corrupted.[![enter image description here](https://stackoverflowteams.com/c/kwikid/images/s/9547fba7-22c8-412f-9f2f-c4b00ddf685c.png)](https://stackoverflowteams.com/c/kwikid/images/s/9547fba7-22c8-412f-9f2f-c4b00ddf685c.png)

- Inform the clients to redo the VKYC for the corrupted sessions.

- Post confirmation change the session_status of the session:

  - Run the below command in `t4-dev` server and replace \<session_id\> with the actual session_id:

    [![enter image description here](https://stackoverflowteams.com/c/kwikid/images/s/6edf4fc1-53bb-4280-be85-adc94f669174.png)](https://stackoverflowteams.com/c/kwikid/images/s/6edf4fc1-53bb-4280-be85-adc94f669174.png)

    ```
    aws dynamodb update-item --table-name kwikid_vkyc_session_status --key '{"session_id": {"S": "<session_id>"}}' --update-expression "SET session_status = :val" --expression-attribute-values '{":val": {"S": "kyc_result_rejected"}}' --endpoint-url https://mio.tc.vkyc.getkwikid.com/dynamo/ --no-verify-ssl
    ```

title: unity | uat | steps to restart services
bodyMarkdown: How to restart services post `Patching activities` or `server reboot`?
body: How to restart services post Patching activities or server reboot?

bodyMarkdown:
Generally, all the services & docker container restarts post server reboot. Following are the steps to check & restart the services, if found down.

----------

# Services:

1. List of all services: `sudo systemctl list-units --type=service`

   [![enter image description here](https://stackoverflowteams.com/c/kwikid/images/s/9dcea02f-f81e-4903-b281-4d817621c4cf.png)](https://stackoverflowteams.com/c/kwikid/images/s/9dcea02f-f81e-4903-b281-4d817621c4cf.png)

2. The service in red is failed ones. Restart by using the command: `sudo systemctl restart <service-name>`. Replace \<service-name\> with the actual service name.  
   Eg.: `sudo systemctl restart kwikid_poc_admin.service`

3. Check status of the server using command: `sudo systemctl status<service-name>`

   Eg.: `sudo systemctl status kwikid_poc_admin.service`

   [![enter image description here](https://stackoverflowteams.com/c/kwikid/images/s/200f83d7-a51d-4894-ae35-cdf62e657dee.png)](https://stackoverflowteams.com/c/kwikid/images/s/200f83d7-a51d-4894-ae35-cdf62e657dee.png)

4. If the service is still not running, check the permissions of the folder:

   1. Using the status command, get the path of the service file.

      [![enter image description here](https://stackoverflowteams.com/c/kwikid/images/s/6493c8d4-34a5-4c9b-a564-0811f360db68.png)](https://stackoverflowteams.com/c/kwikid/images/s/6493c8d4-34a5-4c9b-a564-0811f360db68.png)

   2. Open the service file, get the service working directory path & the user, owner.

      [![enter image description here](https://stackoverflowteams.com/c/kwikid/images/s/489c3f61-b75f-4242-8054-fa7b265f9fa8.png)](https://stackoverflowteams.com/c/kwikid/images/s/489c3f61-b75f-4242-8054-fa7b265f9fa8.png)

   3. To get the owner & user of the working directory, run the command: `ls -ld <working_directory_path>`

      Eg.: `ls -ld /home/ubuntu/Kwikid_ipv_poc/admin-portal-backend`

      [![enter image description here](https://stackoverflowteams.com/c/kwikid/images/s/cf3db2d8-f835-4c6b-93e9-38d76d01c131.png)](https://stackoverflowteams.com/c/kwikid/images/s/cf3db2d8-f835-4c6b-93e9-38d76d01c131.png)

   4. If the owner/user mentioned in the service file is not same as from the above command, change the user & owner to the one mentioned in the service file using command:

      1. `sudo chmod -R 755 <working_directory_path>`

         Replace the `<working_directory_path>` with the WorkingDirectory path mentioned in the service file.

         Eg.: `sudo chmod -R 755 /home/ubuntu/Kwikid_ipv_poc/admin-portal-backend`

      2. `sudo chown -R <owner_name>:<user_name> <working_directory_path>`

   5. Restart the service file & check its status.

---

# Docker

1. Run the command `docker ps -a`, and check for the Exited containers, copy that container_id or container_name.

2. Before restarting, confirm if the similar docker container is not up like previous or new versions in container name (eg. kwikid-admin-api-latest-v5, kwikid-agent-api-v2, etc) or if the api-call is redirecting to the stopped container.

3. Restart the stopped container by using the command: `docker restart <container_id_or_name>`. Replace the `<container_id_or_name>` with the actual container's id or name.

----------

# Docker-Compose

5. More Commands:

Services:

    1. Using the status command, get the path of the service file.

body: Client has given a branch master list in excel format, with X rows and 42 columns. We need to update it into CBI's both backend and frontend services.

bodyMarkdown:
We would have to update the branch master at 2 places in backend and at a single place on minio, UAT/PROD whichever necessary.  
Make sure you have pandas and openpyxl installed before proceeding.

**For Backend,**  
We have to update at 2 places, namely apk/user and dkyc-user. Since the client shares the branch master data in `.xlsx` format, we've to convert it first to `.csv`

1. Convert the .xlsx file to .csv using the below conversion script.

   ```
   import pandas as pd
   
   # Load the Excel file
   xlsx_file = 'TA branch master NOV 2024.xlsx' # Replace with your Excel file name
   sheet_name = 'branch_master_data'            # Replace with your sheet name if necessary
   
   # Read the Excel sheet
   df = pd.read_excel(xlsx_file, sheet_name=sheet_name)
   
   # Save as CSV
   csv_file = 'branch_master_data.csv'          # DONOT change the output file name 
   df.to_csv(csv_file, index=False)
   
   print(f"Excel file has been converted to {csv_file}")
   
   ```

   **Note** : DONOT open the csv file once it has been converted.

2. Upload the output `branch_master_data.csv` file to

   a. apk backend inside `app/` directory

   b. cbs-wrapper inside `data/` directory

3. Restart both the containers/services.  
     
   **Refer below for locations of the above codebases on server**:  
   UAT SERVER APP - (10.1.7.175) -\> 

   apk backend - /data/VKYC/Kwikid_ipv_poc_vkyc/backend/kwikid_poc_apk_backend

   cbs-wrapper - /data/VKYC/Kwikid_ipv_poc_vkyc/backend/kwikid-dkyc-user-api-uat

   PROD SERVER APP1 - (10.1.43.55) -\>  
   apk backend - /data/VKYC/Kwikid_ipv_poc/kwikid_vkyc_apk_backend  
   PROD SERVER APP2 - (10.1.43.56) -\>   
   cbs-wrapper - /data/VKYC/Kwikid_ipv_poc/kwikid_vkyc_cbs_wrapper

**For MINIO,**

We have to convert the `.xlsx` format to state-wise json files. There are a total of 35 files collective of states and uts.

1. Generate the 35 state-wise json files using the below python script. Make sure you pass the correct filename in the `excel_filename` var.

   ```
   # Mapping of state names to dynamic filenames, since state names within the sheet and output filenames 
   # of respective state doesnt match.
   # Hence the keys denote the "State Name" that is stored within the columns of the sheet.
   # And the values are the state names which would be the output for filename for a particular state.
   
   # Eg. In the sheet under "State Name" we have "nct of delhi(ut)" but the output file is named "nct_of_delhi.json"
   state_mapping = {
       "assam" : "assam",
       "meghalaya" : "meghalaya",
       "bihar" : "bihar",
       "jharkhand" : "jharkhand",
       "west bengal" : "west_bengal",
       "odisha" : "orissa",
       "uttar pradesh" : "uttar_pradesh",
       "maharashtra" : "maharashtra",
       "uttarakhand" : "uttarakhand",
       "nct of delhi(ut)" : "nct_of_delhi",
       "punjab" : "punjab",
       "haryana" : "haryana",
       "chandigarh(ut)" : "chandigarh",
       "jammu&kashmir(ut)" : "jammu_and_kashmir",
       "himachalpradesh" : "himachal_pradesh",
       "rajasthan" : "rajasthan",
       "gujarat" : "gujarat",
       "goa" : "goa",
       "union territory of dadra/nagar haveli/diu/daman" : "dadra_and_nagar_haveli_and_daman_and_diu",
       "madhya pradesh" : "madhya_pradesh",
       "chhattisgarh" : "chhattisgarh",
       "telangana state" : "telangana",
       "andhra pradesh" : "andhra_pradesh",
       "karnataka" : "karnataka",
       "tamil nadu" : "tamil_nadu",
       "kerala" : "kerala",
       "pondicherry(ut)" : "puducherry",
       "tripura" : "tripura",
       "manipur" : "manipur",
       "sikkim" : "sikkim",
       "nagaland" : "nagaland",
       "arunachalpradesh" : "arunachal_pradesh",
       "mizoram" : "mizoram",
       "andaman&nicobar(ut)" : "andaman_and_nicobar_islands",
       "ladakh (ut)" : "ladakh",
       "himachal pradesh" : "himachal_pradesh",
       "telangana" : "telangana",
   }
   
   from datetime import date, datetime
   import pandas as pd
   import json
   import os
   excel_filename = 'TA branch master NOV 2024.xlsx'
   # Custom JSON serializer function
   def json_serial(obj):
       if isinstance(obj, (datetime, date)):
           return obj.strftime('%d-%m-%Y')  # Custom date format as per date mapped within the sheet received by CBI.
       raise TypeError(f"Type {type(obj)} not serializable")
   
   # Read the Excel file into a pandas DataFrame
   df = pd.read_excel(excel_filename)
   
   # Specify the selected columns that should be interpreted as strings
   selected_columns_as_strings = ["BSR CODE", "CISBI STATE CODE", "PIN CODE", "MCD-CENSUS 2011", "UBD(Yes)-Census 2011", 
                                  "UBD IN UB STATE-CENSUS 2011", "UBD IN OTHER STATES-Census 2011",
                                  "URC(OLD)", "UBD(Yes)-OLD", "UBD IN UB STATE-OLD", "UBD IN OTHER STATES-OLD", "NEW LINK OFF",
                                  "MCD(OLD DATA)", "PHONE NO", "MOBILE NO"]
   
   # Convert selected columns to string and handle NaN as empty strings
   df[selected_columns_as_strings] = df[selected_columns_as_strings].fillna('').astype(str)
   
   # Fill NaN values with empty strings for all columns
   df = df.fillna('')
   
   # Group the DataFrame by "State Name"
   grouped = df.groupby('State Name')
   
   # Ensure the output directory exists
   output_dir = 'branchList'
   os.makedirs(output_dir, exist_ok=True)
   
   # Loop over each group and write to a separate JSON file

import json

    if isinstance(obj, (datetime, date)):
        return obj.strftime('%d-%m-%Y')  # Custom date format as per date mapped within the sheet received by CBI.
    raise TypeError(f"Type {type(obj)} not serializable")

# Read the Excel file into a pandas DataFrame

# Specify the selected columns that should be interpreted as strings

# Fill NaN values with empty strings for all columns

# Group the DataFrame by "State Name"

# Ensure the output directory exists

# Loop over each group and write to a separate JSON file
for state, group in grouped:

title: Debugging Nginx Port 8000 Service Connection Issues - Unity DKYC service down error
bodyMarkdown: Debugging Nginx Port 8000 Service Connection Issues - Unity DKYC service down error
body: Debugging Nginx Port 8000 Service Connection Issues - Unity DKYC service down error

bodyMarkdown:
**Problem:** Connection refused error when accessing service on port 8000/5001

**Troubleshooting Steps:**

1. Check running processes on port 8000:

```
ps aux | grep "8000" 
netstat -tuln | grep 8000 
sudo lsof -i :8000
```

This showed nginx listening on port 8000

2. Find nginx configuration:

```
sudo grep -r "listen.*8000" /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/
```

Found in `/etc/nginx/sites-enabled/kwikid_poc_dkyc`

3. Inspect configuration:

```
sudo cat /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/kwikid_poc_dkyc
```

Revealed proxy to localhost:5001

4. Check service status:

```
sudo find /etc/systemd/system -type f -exec grep -l "5001" {} \;
sudo systemctl status kwikid_poc_dkyc.service
```

Service was inactive

**Solution:** Start the service:

```
sudo systemctl start kwikid_poc_dkyc.service
```

title: New SSL Certificate details does not reflect in CBI
bodyMarkdown: If you’ve updated the SSL certificate for your domain on NGINX configuration but the new details aren’t reflecting, below answer could be the primary reason for it.
body: If you’ve updated the SSL certificate for your domain on NGINX configuration but the new details aren’t reflecting, below answer could be the primary reason for it.

bodyMarkdown:
3 levels of updation are required when dealing with CBI's network.  
  
1\. **NGINX Configuration** - Pointing ssl to new locations.

2\. **WAF Configuration** -

1. Contact your client or Mac from CBI to ensure the WAF is updated with the new certificate.

2. Confirm that the WAF’s SSL configuration matches your updated server setup.

3. WAF is different for DR and DC as well as UAT and PROD, so ensure the above changes which are to be done are intimated to the client.

3\. **Clear DNS Resolver Cache** - On CBI's intranet it should start reflecting at this point but if it still doesnt then try clearing cache using, `ipconfig /flushdns`.
body:
3 levels of updation are required when dealing with CBI's network.

1. NGINX Configuration - Pointing ssl to new locations.

2. WAF Configuration -

  1. Contact your client or Mac from CBI to ensure the WAF is updated with the new certificate.

  2. Confirm that the WAF’s SSL configuration matches your updated server setup.

  3. WAF is different for DR and DC as well as UAT and PROD, so ensure the above changes which are to be done are intimated to the client.

3. Clear DNS Resolver Cache - On CBI's intranet it should start reflecting at this point but if it still doesnt then try clearing cache using, ipconfig /flushdns.

body:
Reason for all server going down.

# canara.prod.vkyc.app.base server space is full.

bodyMarkdown:
Steps to follow :-

1\. First check server space of "canara.prod.vkyc.app.base" --\> df -lh

2.if space is more than 90%   then run following  on app.base server  "/usr/bin/python3 /home/ubuntu/Kwikid_ipv_poc/clear_docker_container_logs.py"   then check server space after that. with df -lh

3.open agent portal if portal is working do one test call

if still you are getting "504" on agent /admin

4\. restart the nginx --\> sudo systemctl restart nginx.service   then check status with  sudo systemctl status nginx.service

5\. If server in not able to access then go to AWS --\>  ec2 --\>  instance

Select canara.prod.vkyc.app.base.dc instance state option will be there on Top right select that in that Click on stop , check instance state (if stopping then wait) after stopped then again select instance and start this time . IF instance is not able to stop please Dont mark any thing and try to stop forcefully instead try step 6.

6.if instance is not able to stop then --\> Select instance  --\> Action on top right --\> Instance setting --\> change stop protection --\> there disable stop protection and follow step 5.

5.Asana ticket https://app.asana.com/0/inbox/1207264103385199/1209137956242914/1209137956242932

Steps to follow :-

vi VaultAPI.java

private static String API_URL = "https://avaultuat.unitybank.co.in/vault/insert";

The Vault API runs as a standalone service. You can check its status using:

```
systemctl status kwikid_cbs_vault_api.service

For detailed logs:

journalctl -u kwikid_cbs_vault_api.service

URL: https://avaultuat.unitybank.co.in/vault/insert

    "total_pages":1,

}

### Important Security Notes:

title: How to up an kwikid-vkyc-bob-prod-admin-api services
bodyMarkdown:
```
Steps to Verify and Restart Services:
1. Verify and Restart the Admin Backend Server

	Navigate to the bob.prod.dockerize.api.temp directory.
	Check if the admin-backend server is running using the following command
		docker ps
	If the container is not running, restart it with the commands below:
		docker restart CONTAINER_ID_OR_NAME
		sudo systemctl restart docker

2. Check and Restart Load Balancer Instances

	- Access the AWS Management Console and navigate to the load balancers section.
		-Select the bob-prod-dockerize-api-lb load balancer.
		-Open the target group associated with this load balancer: bob-prod-dockerize-api-admin.
		-Identify the instances linked to the target group.
		-Restart the instances via the AWS Console or connect to the servers using PuTTY to access the CLI and restart manually.
                For accessing cli you need pem file which you will get in sharepoint or ask to team member.

3. Test and Reload NGINX on DR and DC Servers

	Access the DR and DC servers.
	Test the NGINX configuration to ensure it is valid:
		sudo nginx -t
	Reload the NGINX configuration to apply any updates:
		sudo nginx -s reload
```
