title: Clickhouse server clean-up
bodyMarkdown:
Server cleanup for following server on UptimeKuma:

[![enter image description here](https://stackoverflowteams.com/c/kwikid/images/s/9c909859-bd9e-4b31-a9b9-6d0a9446d109.png)](https://stackoverflowteams.com/c/kwikid/images/s/9c909859-bd9e-4b31-a9b9-6d0a9446d109.png)
body: Server cleanup for following server on UptimeKuma:

bodyMarkdown:
1. Server name on Teleport: **kwikid.prod.clickhouse**

2. Execute following command on Clickhouse's play application: http://ch.getkwikid.com:8123/play

   ```
   SELECT 
       table, 
       formatReadableSize(sum(data_compressed_bytes)) AS total_size
   FROM system.parts
   WHERE active = 1 GROUP BY table;
   
   ```

   [![enter image description here](https://stackoverflowteams.com/c/kwikid/images/s/84f7752b-70f7-41ca-992f-754e98e89f1a.png)](https://stackoverflowteams.com/c/kwikid/images/s/84f7752b-70f7-41ca-992f-754e98e89f1a.png)

3. Mostly "**trace_log**" and "**query_log**" is consuming more space

4. Run following command to truncate this logs

   **ALTER TABLE system.trace_log DELETE WHERE event_date \< toDate(now() - INTERVAL 3 DAY);**

   **ALTER TABLE system.query_log DELETE WHERE event_date \< toDate(now() - INTERVAL 3 DAY);**

5. Now run following command to optimize this log tables:

   **OPTIMIZE TABLE system.trace_log FINAL;**

   **OPTIMIZE TABLE system.query_log FINAL;**

6. Now wait for few minutes, server space will be auto cleared.
body:
1. Server name on Teleport: kwikid.prod.clickhouse

  2. Execute following command on Clickhouse's play application: http://ch.getkwikid.com:8123/play

    SELECT 
    table, 
    formatReadableSize(sum(data_compressed_bytes)) AS total_size
FROM system.parts
WHERE active = 1 GROUP BY table;

  3. Mostly "trace_log" and "query_log" is consuming more space

  4. Run following command to truncate this logs

    ALTER TABLE system.trace_log DELETE WHERE event_date < toDate(now() - INTERVAL 3 DAY);

    ALTER TABLE system.query_log DELETE WHERE event_date < toDate(now() - INTERVAL 3 DAY);

  5. Now run following command to optimize this log tables:

    OPTIMIZE TABLE system.trace_log FINAL;

    OPTIMIZE TABLE system.query_log FINAL;

  6. Now wait for few minutes, server space will be auto cleared.

cd script

This step must be completed before running the script:

vi user_ids.txt

    • Local Disk D

    • Minio → Data → Sumati folder → [Current file date, e.g., 27.01.205]

title: Clearing podman/docker logs on MSR Server for freeing up server space
bodyMarkdown:
For CBI (MSR IP: 10.1.135.154),   
  
Server space choked due to container logs being written to mounted overlay, 

[![enter image description here](https://stackoverflowteams.com/c/kwikid/images/s/cbde2f73-2583-44fb-b079-afbb0682d4b7.png)](https://stackoverflowteams.com/c/kwikid/images/s/cbde2f73-2583-44fb-b079-afbb0682d4b7.png)
body:
For CBI (MSR IP: 10.1.135.154),

Server space choked due to container logs being written to mounted overlay,

bodyMarkdown:
1. Find the top 5 log files which consume the most space in the podman's mount location.

   `find /var/lib/containers -type f -name "*.log" -exec du -h {} + | sort -rh | head -n 5`

   [![enter image description here](https://stackoverflowteams.com/c/kwikid/images/s/7ce3ebfd-4b83-4d9e-a5d6-7925f5c15337.png)](https://stackoverflowteams.com/c/kwikid/images/s/7ce3ebfd-4b83-4d9e-a5d6-7925f5c15337.png)

2. Check which of the files consume the most space. Then truncate the files one by one using the path as shown in above image.   
   `truncate -s 0 <log_file_path>`

   Note: If files are larger than 10GB, truncation may take a couple of minutes, so be patient.
body:
1. Find the top 5 log files which consume the most space in the podman's mount location.

    find /var/lib/containers -type f -name "*.log" -exec du -h {} + | sort -rh | head -n 5

  2. Check which of the files consume the most space. Then truncate the files one by one using the path as shown in above image.
    truncate -s 0 <log_file_path>

    Note: If files are larger than 10GB, truncation may take a couple of minutes, so be patient.

title: What's the process to debug Unity Event Task Binder callbacks using a mock callback URL?
bodyMarkdown: What's the process to debug Unity Event Task Binder callbacks using a mock callback URL?
body: What's the process to debug Unity Event Task Binder callbacks using a mock callback URL?

bodyMarkdown:
## Overview

This guide outlines the troubleshooting steps for callback-related issues in the KwikID system. Callbacks are triggered for the following events:Callback is sent on 2-3 events 

1. kyc_result_rejected

2. kyc_result_approved

3. kyc_checker_approved (Auditor Approved)

4. kyc_checker_rejected (Auditor Rejected)

## Initial Verification Steps

### 1. Check S3 Logs

Verify if callback files exist in the appropriate S3 bucket:

**Production Environment**

- Bucket: kwikid-prod

- Path: videokyc/logs/callback/unity/{user_id}/{session_id}/

**UAT Environment**

- Bucket: kwikid-uat

- Path: videokyc/logs/callback/unity_uat/{user_id}/{session_id}/

Note: The presence of files in S3 doesn't guarantee successful callback delivery. Further investigation may be needed.

### 2. Client Verification

Share the logs with the client to confirm if they received the callbacks.

## Advanced Troubleshooting

### 1. Flagsmith Configuration Check

If callbacks aren't being received:

1. Navigate to Flagsmith

2. Access Users section

3. Search for client name (e.g., unity_uat)

4. Look for "notification" settings

5. Review complete configuration for event task binder events

### 2. Service Status Check

Note the different deployment models:

- UAT: Event task binder and notification service run as Docker containers

- Production: Services run as system services

Commands for Docker environments:

```
# List running containers 
docker ps 
# Check service 
logs docker logs [container_name]
```

### 3. API Verification

Reference: docs.getkwikid.com/tools

Key APIs to check:

1. bind-task API

   - Verify 200 response code

   - Check complete payload in [bind-task-api-doc](https://thinkanalyticsindia.sharepoint.com/:t:/s/KwikIDDocumentaion/EfpFlJvDvwNAnBPk-CCkX80BLPbvBSDSxASv0k1r2FM4TQ?e=jpx0Hm)

2. bind-task/synchronous API

   - Responsible for callback triggers

   - Validates product_code against Flagsmith

   - Reference: [bind-task-synchronous-api-doc](https://stackoverflowteams.com/c/kwikid/images/s/a2d6179a-1bc6-400c-a490-97ea8b0a6365.png)

### 4. Environment Configuration

Check Redis environment files:

1. Use `docker inspect` to locate env file paths

2. Verify environment variables match expected values

## Testing with Mock API

### Setup Test Environment

1. Create mock endpoint at beeceptor.com

2. Add test URL to Flagsmith config as fallback

3. Note: Include "preop" keyword if needed for accurate client response simulation

### Connectivity Testing

If other steps pass but callbacks still fail:

1. Ping callback URL from UAT server

2. Perform telnet test to verify connectivity

## Common Issues

- Missing or incorrect callback URL configuration

- Environment file misconfigurations

- Network connectivity issues

- Product code mismatches in Flagsmith

- Redis configuration problems

## Best Practices

- Always verify S3 logs first

- Get client confirmation of non-receipt

- Check service status before deep diving

- Use mock endpoints for validation

- Document all troubleshooting steps taken

  4. kyc_checker_rejected (Auditor Rejected)

Initial Verification Steps

1. Check S3 Logs

Verify if callback files exist in the appropriate S3 bucket:

Production Environment

  • Bucket: kwikid-prod

  • Path: videokyc/logs/callback/unity/{user_id}/{session_id}/

UAT Environment

  • Bucket: kwikid-uat

  • Path: videokyc/logs/callback/unity_uat/{user_id}/{session_id}/

Note: The presence of files in S3 doesn't guarantee successful callback delivery. Further investigation may be needed.

2. Client Verification

Share the logs with the client to confirm if they received the callbacks.

Advanced Troubleshooting

1. Flagsmith Configuration Check

If callbacks aren't being received:

  1. Navigate to Flagsmith

  2. Access Users section

  3. Search for client name (e.g., unity_uat)

  4. Look for "notification" settings

  5. Review complete configuration for event task binder events

2. Service Status Check

Note the different deployment models:

  • UAT: Event task binder and notification service run as Docker containers

  • Production: Services run as system services

Commands for Docker environments:

# List running containers 
docker ps 
# Check service 
logs docker logs [container_name]

3. API Verification

Reference: docs.getkwikid.com/tools

Key APIs to check:

  1. bind-task API

    • Verify 200 response code

    • Check complete payload in bind-task-api-doc

  2. bind-task/synchronous API

    • Responsible for callback triggers

    • Validates product_code against Flagsmith

    • Reference: bind-task-synchronous-api-doc

4. Environment Configuration

Check Redis environment files:

  1. Use docker inspect to locate env file paths

  2. Verify environment variables match expected values

Testing with Mock API

Setup Test Environment

  1. Create mock endpoint at beeceptor.com

  2. Add test URL to Flagsmith config as fallback

  3. Note: Include "preop" keyword if needed for accurate client response simulation

Connectivity Testing

If other steps pass but callbacks still fail:

  1. Ping callback URL from UAT server

  2. Perform telnet test to verify connectivity

Common Issues

  • Missing or incorrect callback URL configuration

  • Environment file misconfigurations

  • Network connectivity issues

  • Product code mismatches in Flagsmith

  • Redis configuration problems

Best Practices

  • Always verify S3 logs first

  • Get client confirmation of non-receipt

  • Check service status before deep diving

  • Use mock endpoints for validation

  • Document all troubleshooting steps taken

title: How to Monitor Celery Tasks and RabbitMQ Queues in Our System for Unity?
bodyMarkdown: How to Monitor Celery Tasks and RabbitMQ Queues in Our System for Unity ?
body: How to Monitor Celery Tasks and RabbitMQ Queues in Our System for Unity ?

bodyMarkdown:
## System Overview

Our system uses Celery with RabbitMQ as the message broker. Here are the key components:

- **Celery Workers**: Running on `kwikid_vkyc_unity` and `kwikid_vkyc_unity_al` queues

- **RabbitMQ Server**: Located at `172.29.22.74:5672`

- **Celery Tasks**: Including merge_blobs, create_zip_file, and other IPV-related tasks

## 1. Checking Running Celery Workers

To see all running Celery workers:

```
ps aux | grep celery
```

Our main workers are:

```
# Main worker with concurrency 2
celery worker -A celery_app.app -Q kwikid_vkyc_unity --loglevel=info -c 2

# Secondary worker with concurrency 1
celery worker -A celery_app.app -Q kwikid_vkyc_unity_al --loglevel=info -c 1
```

## 2. Monitoring Celery Tasks

### View Registered Tasks

```
# Activate virtual environment
source /home/ubuntu/Kwikid_ipv_poc/venv/bin/activate

# Navigate to application directory
cd /home/ubuntu/Kwikid_ipv_poc/kwikid_ipv_backend_new

# List all registered tasks
celery -A celery_app.app inspect registered -d worker@ip-172-29-22-165
```

### Check Task Logs

```
# Main worker logs
tail -f /home/ubuntu/Kwikid_ipv_poc/celery_poc.logs

# Secondary worker logs
tail -f /home/ubuntu/Kwikid_ipv_poc/celery_poc_al.logs

# Filter for specific tasks
tail -f /home/ubuntu/Kwikid_ipv_poc/celery_poc.logs | grep "merge_blobs"
```

## 3. RabbitMQ Monitoring

### Web Management Interface

1. Access URL: `http://172.29.22.74:15672`

2. Login credentials:

   - Username: `rmq_unity_admin`

   - Password: `Tan1234$`

3. Features available:

   - Queue monitoring

   - Message rates

   - Active connections

   - Consumer status

### Command Line Monitoring

Install and use rabbitmqadmin:

```
# Download rabbitmqadmin
wget http://172.29.22.74:15672/cli/rabbitmqadmin
chmod +x rabbitmqadmin

# List queues
./rabbitmqadmin -H 172.29.22.74 -P 15672 -u rmq_unity_admin -p 'Tan1234$' list queues

# List connections
./rabbitmqadmin -H 172.29.22.74 -P 15672 -u rmq_unity_admin -p 'Tan1234$' list connections
```

## 4. Task Status Checking

### Check Specific Task Status

Using Redis (if configured):

```
redis-cli
> get celery-task-meta-[task-id]
```

Example output for a failed task:

```
{
    "status": "FAILURE",
    "traceback": "Traceback details...",
    "result": {
        "exc_message": ["error details"],
        "exc_type": "ErrorType"
    },
    "task_id": "task-id"
}
```

## Common Issues and Troubleshooting

1. Task Not Found:

   - Check if worker is running

   - Verify correct queue assignment

   - Check task registration

2. Failed Tasks:

   - Check celery logs for error details

   - Verify file permissions if IO related

   - Check network connectivity for external services

3. Worker Connection Issues:

   - Verify RabbitMQ service is running

   - Check network connectivity

   - Verify credentials are correct

## Best Practices

1. Regular Monitoring:

   - Check worker status daily

   - Monitor queue lengths

   - Review error logs

2. Queue Management:

   - Keep track of task distribution

   - Monitor task completion times

   - Check for stuck tasks

3. Resource Management:

   - Monitor worker memory usage

   - Check CPU utilization

   - Review disk space for logs

## Additional Resources

- [Celery Documentation](https://docs.celeryproject.org/)

- [RabbitMQ Management Guide](https://www.rabbitmq.com/management.html)

title: How to Reset Login Locks for RBL Agent/Admin Accounts in DynamoDB through AWS CLI
bodyMarkdown:
My agents/admins are getting locked out of the RBL system and need to reset these DynamoDB login counters:

- login_lock (default = 0)

- login (default = 0)

- login_attempts (default = 0)

Common scenarios when reset is needed:

1. Users exceed maximum login attempts

2. Sessions get stuck in a locked state

3. Admin accounts become inaccessible
body:
My agents/admins are getting locked out of the RBL system and need to reset these DynamoDB login counters:

  • login_lock (default = 0)

  • login (default = 0)

  • login_attempts (default = 0)

Common scenarios when reset is needed:

  1. Users exceed maximum login attempts

  2. Sessions get stuck in a locked state

  3. Admin accounts become inaccessible

bodyMarkdown:
Here's the AWS CLI command to reset all login counters to default values:

```
aws dynamodb update-item \
    --table-name kwikid_vkyc_agent \
    --key '{"client_name": {"S": "RBL"}, "agent_id": {"S": "RBL_admin"}}' \
    --update-expression "SET login_lock = :ll, login_attempts = :la, login = :lg" \
    --expression-attribute-values '{":ll": {"N": "0"}, ":la": {"N": "0"}, ":lg": {"N": "0"}}' \
    --return-values ALL_NEW
```

***Important Notes:***

1. **Server Requirements**:

   - ✅ Run only on `.62` or `.4` servers

   - ❌ Other servers will throw permission errors

2. **Required Changes**:

   - Update `agent_id` with the specific user ID

   - Verify `client_name` matches your domain

3. **Use Cases**:

   - Reset after exceeding login attempts

   - Unlock stuck login sessions

   - Restore admin access in emergencies

Below is the detailed step-by-step solution I worked out.
body:
I recently needed to re-trigger callbacks for RBL's UAT Domains that go through Event Task Binder. After figuring out the process, I'm documenting it here for others who might face the same requirement.

Environment Context:

  • UAT Server accessible via teleport (rbl.uat.app.vkyc)
  • Docker container running agent API (kwikid-vkyc-agent-api)
  • Docker image: 740186269845.dkr.ecr.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/kwikid-vkyc-agent-api
  • Python script for re-triggering: retrigger_irctc_callback.py

Below is the detailed step-by-step solution I worked out.

bodyMarkdown:
1. Login to RBL's UAT server through teleport:

   ```bash
   rbl.uat.app.vkyc
   ```

2. Check running docker:

   ```bash
   docker ps
   ```

   Find the docker id for image: `740186269845.dkr.ecr.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/kwikid-vkyc-agent-api` and container name `kwikid-vkyc-agent-api`

   [![Docker PS Output](https://stackoverflowteams.com/c/kwikid/images/s/aeea44fc-16e8-431e-a580-3353e3068700.png)](https://stackoverflowteams.com/c/kwikid/images/s/aeea44fc-16e8-431e-a580-3353e3068700.png)

3. Inspect the docker file to find the mounted folder:

   ```bash
   docker inspect kwikid-vkyc-agent-api | grep "Mounts" -A 9
   ```

   Copy the Source's value which is the folder containing the codebase.

   [![Docker Inspect Output](https://stackoverflowteams.com/c/kwikid/images/s/f75d97f5-7c41-4e6b-8262-bbcef46ccb29.png)](https://stackoverflowteams.com/c/kwikid/images/s/f75d97f5-7c41-4e6b-8262-bbcef46ccb29.png)

4. Go to the highlighted directory with the command:

   ```bash
   cd /var/lib/docker/volumes/vcip-user_ipv_api/_data
   ```

   List the files:

   ```bash
   ls | grep "retrigger"
   ```

   You should see a file called `retrigger_irctc_callback.py`

   [![Directory Contents](https://stackoverflowteams.com/c/kwikid/images/s/29e22616-9851-4a63-8114-21c4d80aae9f.png)](https://stackoverflowteams.com/c/kwikid/images/s/29e22616-9851-4a63-8114-21c4d80aae9f.png)

5. Open the file using vim or vi editor:

   ```bash
   vim retrigger_irctc_callback.py
   ```

   Change the following parameters as per requirement:

   - session_id
   - user_id
   - event_name
   - domain

   [![File Contents](https://stackoverflowteams.com/c/kwikid/images/s/11c64924-0a23-4c26-98b7-b9b9323b3a13.png)](https://stackoverflowteams.com/c/kwikid/images/s/11c64924-0a23-4c26-98b7-b9b9323b3a13.png)

6. The saved file has to be run from inside the docker due to presence of python executor:

   ```bash
   docker exec -it kwikid-vkyc-agent-api python retrigger_irctc_callback.py
   ```

   This command will execute and show logs outputs:

   [![Execution Logs](https://stackoverflowteams.com/c/kwikid/images/s/bb11b2ba-e34e-488b-9ecc-dbc72884dae4.png)](https://stackoverflowteams.com/c/kwikid/images/s/bb11b2ba-e34e-488b-9ecc-dbc72884dae4.png)

7. At the end, a task id should be printed which shows that callback is triggered successfully:

   [![Task ID Output](https://stackoverflowteams.com/c/kwikid/images/s/3e4bf50a-a467-42d4-81f3-c7d14c9ad4eb.png)](https://stackoverflowteams.com/c/kwikid/images/s/3e4bf50a-a467-42d4-81f3-c7d14c9ad4eb.png)

----------

**Important Note:** The task ID confirms successful callback initiation from our end. However, the actual acceptance and processing by the receiving application needs to be verified separately as it's outside our system's scope.

4. scope 2.colending

5. scope 3.account_opening

bodyMarkdown:
**EMSIGNER CREDENTIALS CONFIGURATION**

Steps to configure the Emsigner Credentials for Spark Capital -

1. Go To Flagsmit using below link - <https://dev.vkyc.getkwikid.com:8001/project/1/environment/QqrpgZ4n32kZUZ5zDM4FhD/users>

In this, Go to -\> Development \> Users

[![Step 1](https://stackoverflowteams.com/c/kwikid/images/s/baf24cdd-e1ac-482f-b45f-fdceffd3c8ba.png)](https://stackoverflowteams.com/c/kwikid/images/s/baf24cdd-e1ac-482f-b45f-fdceffd3c8ba.png)

2. Search “spark” as shown below which will give a list of spark capital’s domains

[![Step 2](https://stackoverflowteams.com/c/kwikid/images/s/a33e7c11-75bf-4ec9-8bf0-f1cb3d092723.png)](https://stackoverflowteams.com/c/kwikid/images/s/a33e7c11-75bf-4ec9-8bf0-f1cb3d092723.png)

Once you get the mentioned list of Spark Capital domains. Follow the Step 3 for each of the 5 domains. (Why all 5, because initial spark capital was configured on sparkcapital_dev, then sparkcapital_uat and then spark_pwm but all of them had same KMS ID and for which domain that KMS ID was generation, we don’t have documentation currently, so do it for all 5)

Step 3 – Configure the provide credentials

1. Click one domain, for e.g. sparkcapital_dev. It will open the list of services configured.

[![Step 3](https://stackoverflowteams.com/c/kwikid/images/s/aba2ce1f-fd1a-45be-902c-b65b027bb646.png)](https://stackoverflowteams.com/c/kwikid/images/s/aba2ce1f-fd1a-45be-902c-b65b027bb646.png)

2. Click on “kwikid-doc-service". It will open a new code editor from right side.

[![Step 4](https://stackoverflowteams.com/c/kwikid/images/s/4546a4c3-5c37-4d10-ba2c-177eabeeef02.png)](https://stackoverflowteams.com/c/kwikid/images/s/4546a4c3-5c37-4d10-ba2c-177eabeeef02.png)

3. Now click “show more” and scroll to the end where you will find the config for ESIGN. There you can update the credentials. Then below click and “Update Feature” button and it’s done.

4. Follow this for all 5 domains as mentioned.
body:
EMSIGNER CREDENTIALS CONFIGURATION

Steps to configure the Emsigner Credentials for Spark Capital -

  1. Go To Flagsmit using below link - https://dev.vkyc.getkwikid.com:8001/project/1/environment/QqrpgZ4n32kZUZ5zDM4FhD/users

In this, Go to -> Development > Users

  1. Search “spark” as shown below which will give a list of spark capital’s domains

Once you get the mentioned list of Spark Capital domains. Follow the Step 3 for each of the 5 domains. (Why all 5, because initial spark capital was configured on sparkcapital_dev, then sparkcapital_uat and then spark_pwm but all of them had same KMS ID and for which domain that KMS ID was generation, we don’t have documentation currently, so do it for all 5)

Step 3 – Configure the provide credentials

  1. Click one domain, for e.g. sparkcapital_dev. It will open the list of services configured.

  1. Click on “kwikid-doc-service". It will open a new code editor from right side.

  1. Now click “show more” and scroll to the end where you will find the config for ESIGN. There you can update the credentials. Then below click and “Update Feature” button and it’s done.

  2. Follow this for all 5 domains as mentioned.

```

[![enter image description here](https://stackoverflowteams.com/c/kwikid/images/s/1b90e62d-ea9e-47ae-a36a-2ace0a412abd.png)](https://stackoverflowteams.com/c/kwikid/images/s/1b90e62d-ea9e-47ae-a36a-2ace0a412abd.png)

**Note: to check for specific session id, grep session id**

3. if all is successful api hits, check second logs for minio push.

tail -f /home/ubuntu/Shinhan/celery_shinhan.logs

In this example, a single field is defined for the mobile number. **Field Object Details:** - **`default`** *Type:* Object *Purpose:* Specifies a default value (currently an empty object). - **`disabled`** *Type:* Boolean *Purpose:* Indicates whether the field is disabled. *Possible Values:* `true` or `false` - **`key`** *Type:* String *Purpose:* Uniquely identifies the field (here, `"mobile"`). - **`label`** *Type:* Object (Localized strings) *Purpose:* Provides display labels for the field in multiple languages. *Possible Keys/Values:* - `"en": "Mobile Number"` - `"hi": "मोबाइल नंबर"` - `"ka": (Kannada label)` - `"mal": (Malayalam label)` - `"ta": (Tamil label)` - `"tel": (Telugu label)` - **`properties`** *Type:* Object *Purpose:* Sets UI and formatting properties for the field. *Key Properties:* - **`containerStyles`**: CSS styles (e.g., `"margin-bottom: -0.5rem;"`) - **`countryCode`**: A string for the country code (can be empty). - **`phoneMaskAfterCountryCode`**: Format mask (e.g., `"##########"`) - **`placeholder`**: Localized placeholder text prompting the user (supports multiple languages). - **`prefix`** & **`postfix`**: Strings to be added before or after the input. - **`removeCountryCodeFromValue`**: Boolean flag to indicate if the country code should be stripped from the final value. - **`type`** *Type:* String *Purpose:* Specifies the input type for the field. *Example Value:* `"phone"` - **`validation`** *Type:* Object *Purpose:* Provides rules and actions for validating the input. *Key Elements:* - **`actions`**: An array of actions executed during validation. For example, actions can show error messages when conditions are not met or set values upon successful validation. *Possible Conditions & Actions:* - `"NOT(1)"` conditions trigger error display actions with messages like: - `"Language Not Available. Please Refresh Page"` - A condition `"1"` that sets a predefined value for the field’s validation state. - **`rules`**: An array of validation rules. For instance, a rule might check that the input is not empty. *Example:* A rule with an ID (`"12"`) using a key `"VALUE_CHECK"` and a pattern defined by `"IS_NOT_EMPTY"`. This rule may pull data (such as the selected language) from browser storage. - **`triggers`**: An array defining when validation should occur. *Example Values:* `"ON_INIT"`, `"ON_CHANGE"` - **`validators`** *Type:* Object *Purpose:* Additional constraints on the field value. *Key Properties:* - **`minLength`**: Numeric value defining the minimum length (here, `10` digits). - **`required`**: Boolean indicating if the field is mandatory (`true`). ### b. Title **Key:** `title` (Object) - **Purpose:** Provides a localized title for the mobile login section. - **Possible Keys/Values:** - `"en": "Please provide your Aadhaar Linked Mobile Number"` - `"hi": "कृपया अपना आधार लिंक्ड मोबाइल नंबर दें"` - `"ka": (Kannada version)` - `"mal": (Malayalam version)` - `"ta": (Tamil version)` - `"tel": (Telugu version)` ---------- ## 2. Language List **Key:** `langList` - **Purpose:** Defines the list of available languages for the application, supporting multilingual interfaces. - **Each Language Object Contains:** - **`disabled`** *Type:* Boolean *Purpose:* Determines if the language option is currently available. - **`key`** *Type:* String *Purpose:* The language code (e.g., `"en"`, `"hi"`, `"ta"`, `"tel"`, `"ka"`, `"mal"`). - **`label`** *Type:* String *Purpose:* A short text label for the language (for example, `"Search"` for English). - **`placeholder`** (Optional) *Type:* String *Purpose:* Placeholder text used in language search fields. - **`selected`** *Type:* Boolean *Purpose:* Indicates if the language is the default selected option. - **`title`** *Type:* String *Purpose:* Full name or descriptive title of the language (e.g., `"English"`, `"हिंदी (Hindi)"`). ---------- ## 3. Pre-Fill On Login **Key:** `preFillOnLogin` - **Purpose:** Controls the behavior of pre-filling input fields on the login page. - **Properties:** - **`byPassOtp`** *Type:* Boolean *Purpose:* If `true`, bypasses the OTP verification step. - **`enterUserId`** *Type:* Boolean *Purpose:* If `true`, prompts the user to enter a user ID. - **`isText`** *Type:* Boolean *Purpose:* Indicates whether the pre-fill content is plain text. - **`isRedact`** *Type:* Boolean *Purpose:* Specifies if the pre-filled value should be partially hidden (redacted). - **`key`** *Type:* String *Purpose:* Defines which fields are eligible for pre-fill using a pipe-separated string (e.g., `"phone_number|user_id|email"`). ---------- ## 4. Privacy Policy **Key:** `privacyPolicy` - **Purpose:** Configures how the privacy policy is displayed and accessed by users. - **Properties:** - **`displayText`** *Type:* String *Purpose:* The text label for the privacy policy link (e.g., `"Privacy Policy"`). - **`isShow`** *Type:* Boolean *Purpose:* Determines if the privacy policy link should be shown. - **`popup`** *Type:* Object *Purpose:* May contain additional properties for displaying the privacy policy in a popup window. *Example:* Currently contains an empty `"link"`. - **`redirection`** *Type:* Object *Purpose:* Defines how users are redirected when clicking the privacy policy link. - **`link`**: URL for the privacy policy page (placeholder value used here). - **`target`**: Determines how the link is opened (e.g., `"_blank"` opens in a new tab). ---------- ## 5. Theme **Key:** `theme` - **Purpose:** Provides branding and styling options for the application. - **Properties:** - **`clientLogo`** *Type:* String (URL) *Purpose:* URL of the primary client logo. - **`clientName`** *Type:* String *Purpose:* The name of the client organization (e.g., `"CENTRAL BANK OF INDIA"`). - **`colors`** *Type:* Object *Purpose:* Defines the primary and secondary color schemes. - **`primary`**: - **`active`**, **`background`**, **`hover`**, **`text`** *Example Values:* - `"active": "#2a89eb"` - `"background": "#166fc1"` - `"hover": "#6bb2fb"` - `"text": "#fff"` - **`secondary`**: - Similar structure to primary. - **`loginPage`** *Type:* Object *Purpose:* Contains visual assets for the login page. - **Key:** `"image|html|animation"` *Purpose:* Can be a URL pointing to an image, HTML content, or animation to be displayed. - **`poweredByLogo`** *Type:* String (URL) *Purpose:* URL for the “powered by” logo. - **`smallLogo`** *Type:* String (URL) *Purpose:* URL for an alternative, smaller version of the client logo. ---------- ## 6. Terms & Conditions on Start **Key:** `tncOnStart` - **Purpose:** Displays the terms and conditions (T&C) at the start of the user journey, outlining requirements and steps. - **Properties:** - **`listItem`** *Type:* Array of Strings *Purpose:* Contains one or more HTML-formatted strings listing the requirements and steps. *Example:* ```json ["Requirments
a. Valid PPO number.
b. Bank Account number linked to Pension.
c. Aadhaar/PAN Card original.
d. Smart phone/ Tab/ Laptop/ Desk top with internet connectivity and web camera.
e. Valid Mobile Number

2 easy steps to be followed
a. Click a link available in Bank website and provide basic details.
b. Schedule a session or Connect to Bank agent directly. Complete Cent Digi-LC session successfully."] ``` - **`title`** *Type:* String *Purpose:* Title text for the T&C section (e.g., `"Do Paperless Life Certificate submission Through Cent Digi-LC"`). ---------- ## 7. Utility Flags **Key:** `utilityFlags` - **Purpose:** Contains a series of flags and settings that govern various aspects of the frontend behavior, from OTP handling to UI versioning. - **Properties:** - **`agentLoginOtpLength`** *Type:* Number *Purpose:* Defines the OTP length for agent logins (e.g., `6`). - **`bypassLogin`** *Type:* Boolean *Purpose:* If `true`, allows bypassing the login process. - **`bypassOtp`** *Type:* Boolean *Purpose:* If `true`, bypasses OTP verification. - **`dedupeMobileOtp`** *Type:* Number *Purpose:* Indicates deduplication rules/count for mobile OTP (e.g., `1`). - **`hideOtpFieldPlaceholder`** *Type:* Boolean *Purpose:* If `true`, hides the placeholder text in the OTP field. - **`isAgentVerifyOtp`** *Type:* Boolean *Purpose:* Determines if OTP verification by an agent is enabled. - **`isLangSelect`** *Type:* Boolean *Purpose:* Enables language selection on the login page. - **`isPoweredBy`** *Type:* Boolean *Purpose:* Determines if the “powered by” branding is displayed. - **`isPoweredByText`** *Type:* Boolean *Purpose:* Indicates if a text-based “powered by” label should be shown. - **`loginOtpLength`** *Type:* Number *Purpose:* Defines the OTP length for general user login (e.g., `6`). - **`pagesV2`** *Type:* Boolean *Purpose:* Indicates whether version 2 of the UI pages is in use. - **`preLoginInit`** *Type:* Boolean *Purpose:* If `true`, triggers pre-login initialization routines. - **`showAgentDashboard`** *Type:* Boolean *Purpose:* Controls the visibility of the agent dashboard. - **`stageData`** *Type:* Boolean *Purpose:* Indicates whether staged (or test) data should be used. - **`userJourney`** *Type:* Boolean *Purpose:* Enables tracking or customization of the user journey through the login process. ---------- ## Conclusion This configuration file is designed to offer a high degree of customization for your frontend login experience. It allows you to: - Define field behavior and validation for mobile login. - Support multiple languages and customize language options. - Control pre-fill behavior for login forms. - Configure privacy policy access and presentation. - Set up theming and branding with logos and color schemes. - Present terms & conditions dynamically. - Fine-tune miscellaneous behaviors via utility flags. By understanding and adjusting these parameters, developers can ensure a flexible, user-friendly, and branded login process.

1. Login Configuration

Key: loginConfig

This section defines how the login interface behaves—specifically for mobile login in this example.

1.1 Mobile Login

Key: mobileLogin

  • Purpose:
    Configures the mobile login form fields, labels, validation, and UI behavior for users logging in using a mobile number.

  • Sub-sections:

    a. Fields

    Key: fields (Array)

    Each object in the array represents a field used for login. In this example, a single field is defined for the mobile number.

    Field Object Details:

    • default
      Type: Object
      Purpose: Specifies a default value (currently an empty object).

    • disabled
      Type: Boolean
      Purpose: Indicates whether the field is disabled.
      Possible Values: true or false

    • key
      Type: String
      Purpose: Uniquely identifies the field (here, "mobile").

    • label
      Type: Object (Localized strings)
      Purpose: Provides display labels for the field in multiple languages.
      Possible Keys/Values:

      • "en": "Mobile Number"

      • "hi": "मोबाइल नंबर"

      • "ka": (Kannada label)

      • "mal": (Malayalam label)

      • "ta": (Tamil label)

      • "tel": (Telugu label)

    • properties
      Type: Object
      Purpose: Sets UI and formatting properties for the field.
      Key Properties:

      • containerStyles: CSS styles (e.g., "margin-bottom: -0.5rem;")

      • countryCode: A string for the country code (can be empty).

      • phoneMaskAfterCountryCode: Format mask (e.g., "##########")

      • placeholder: Localized placeholder text prompting the user (supports multiple languages).

      • prefix & postfix: Strings to be added before or after the input.

      • removeCountryCodeFromValue: Boolean flag to indicate if the country code should be stripped from the final value.

    • type
      Type: String
      Purpose: Specifies the input type for the field.
      Example Value: "phone"

    • validation
      Type: Object
      Purpose: Provides rules and actions for validating the input.
      Key Elements:

      • actions:
        An array of actions executed during validation. For example, actions can show error messages when conditions are not met or set values upon successful validation.
        Possible Conditions & Actions:

        • "NOT(1)" conditions trigger error display actions with messages like:

          • "Language Not Available. Please Refresh Page"

        • A condition "1" that sets a predefined value for the field’s validation state.

      • rules:
        An array of validation rules. For instance, a rule might check that the input is not empty.
        Example: A rule with an ID ("12") using a key "VALUE_CHECK" and a pattern defined by "IS_NOT_EMPTY". This rule may pull data (such as the selected language) from browser storage.

      • triggers:
        An array defining when validation should occur.
        Example Values: "ON_INIT", "ON_CHANGE"

    • validators
      Type: Object
      Purpose: Additional constraints on the field value.
      Key Properties:

      • minLength: Numeric value defining the minimum length (here, 10 digits).

      • required: Boolean indicating if the field is mandatory (true).

    b. Title

    Key: title (Object)

    • Purpose:
      Provides a localized title for the mobile login section.

    • Possible Keys/Values:

      • "en": "Please provide your Aadhaar Linked Mobile Number"

      • "hi": "कृपया अपना आधार लिंक्ड मोबाइल नंबर दें"

      • "ka": (Kannada version)

      • "mal": (Malayalam version)

      • "ta": (Tamil version)

      • "tel": (Telugu version)

2. Language List

Key: langList

  • Purpose:
    Defines the list of available languages for the application, supporting multilingual interfaces.

  • Each Language Object Contains:

    • disabled
      Type: Boolean
      Purpose: Determines if the language option is currently available.

    • key
      Type: String
      Purpose: The language code (e.g., "en", "hi", "ta", "tel", "ka", "mal").

    • label
      Type: String
      Purpose: A short text label for the language (for example, "Search" for English).

    • placeholder (Optional)
      Type: String
      Purpose: Placeholder text used in language search fields.

    • selected
      Type: Boolean
      Purpose: Indicates if the language is the default selected option.

    • title
      Type: String
      Purpose: Full name or descriptive title of the language (e.g., "English", "हिंदी (Hindi)").

3. Pre-Fill On Login

Key: preFillOnLogin

  • Purpose:
    Controls the behavior of pre-filling input fields on the login page.

  • Properties:

    • byPassOtp
      Type: Boolean
      Purpose: If true, bypasses the OTP verification step.

    • enterUserId
      Type: Boolean
      Purpose: If true, prompts the user to enter a user ID.

    • isText
      Type: Boolean
      Purpose: Indicates whether the pre-fill content is plain text.

    • isRedact
      Type: Boolean
      Purpose: Specifies if the pre-filled value should be partially hidden (redacted).

    • key
      Type: String
      Purpose: Defines which fields are eligible for pre-fill using a pipe-separated string (e.g., "phone_number|user_id|email").

4. Privacy Policy

Key: privacyPolicy

  • Purpose:
    Configures how the privacy policy is displayed and accessed by users.

  • Properties:

    • displayText
      Type: String
      Purpose: The text label for the privacy policy link (e.g., "Privacy Policy").

    • isShow
      Type: Boolean
      Purpose: Determines if the privacy policy link should be shown.

    • popup
      Type: Object
      Purpose: May contain additional properties for displaying the privacy policy in a popup window.
      Example: Currently contains an empty "link".

    • redirection
      Type: Object
      Purpose: Defines how users are redirected when clicking the privacy policy link.

      • link: URL for the privacy policy page (placeholder value used here).

      • target: Determines how the link is opened (e.g., "_blank" opens in a new tab).

5. Theme

Key: theme

  • Purpose:
    Provides branding and styling options for the application.

  • Properties:

    • clientLogo
      Type: String (URL)
      Purpose: URL of the primary client logo.

    • clientName
      Type: String
      Purpose: The name of the client organization (e.g., "CENTRAL BANK OF INDIA").

    • colors
      Type: Object
      Purpose: Defines the primary and secondary color schemes.

      • primary:

        • active, background, hover, text
          Example Values:

          • "active": "#2a89eb"

          • "background": "#166fc1"

          • "hover": "#6bb2fb"

          • "text": "#fff"

      • secondary:

        • Similar structure to primary.

    • loginPage
      Type: Object
      Purpose: Contains visual assets for the login page.

      • Key: "image|html|animation"
        Purpose: Can be a URL pointing to an image, HTML content, or animation to be displayed.

    • poweredByLogo
      Type: String (URL)
      Purpose: URL for the “powered by” logo.

    • smallLogo
      Type: String (URL)
      Purpose: URL for an alternative, smaller version of the client logo.

6. Terms & Conditions on Start

Key: tncOnStart

  • Purpose:
    Displays the terms and conditions (T&C) at the start of the user journey, outlining requirements and steps.

  • Properties:

    • listItem
      Type: Array of Strings
      Purpose: Contains one or more HTML-formatted strings listing the requirements and steps.
      Example:

      ["<b>Requirments</b><br/> a. Valid PPO number.<br/> b. Bank Account number linked to Pension.<br/> c. Aadhaar/PAN Card original.<br/> d. Smart phone/ Tab/ Laptop/ Desk top with internet connectivity and web camera.<br/> e. Valid Mobile Number<br/> <br/> <b>2 easy steps to be followed</b><br/> a. Click a link available in Bank website and provide basic details.<br/> b. Schedule a session or Connect to Bank agent directly. Complete Cent Digi-LC session successfully."]

    • title
      Type: String
      Purpose: Title text for the T&C section (e.g., "Do Paperless Life Certificate submission Through Cent Digi-LC").

7. Utility Flags

Key: utilityFlags

  • Purpose:
    Contains a series of flags and settings that govern various aspects of the frontend behavior, from OTP handling to UI versioning.

  • Properties:

    • agentLoginOtpLength
      Type: Number
      Purpose: Defines the OTP length for agent logins (e.g., 6).

    • bypassLogin
      Type: Boolean
      Purpose: If true, allows bypassing the login process.

    • bypassOtp
      Type: Boolean
      Purpose: If true, bypasses OTP verification.

    • dedupeMobileOtp
      Type: Number
      Purpose: Indicates deduplication rules/count for mobile OTP (e.g., 1).

    • hideOtpFieldPlaceholder
      Type: Boolean
      Purpose: If true, hides the placeholder text in the OTP field.

    • isAgentVerifyOtp
      Type: Boolean
      Purpose: Determines if OTP verification by an agent is enabled.

    • isLangSelect
      Type: Boolean
      Purpose: Enables language selection on the login page.

    • isPoweredBy
      Type: Boolean
      Purpose: Determines if the “powered by” branding is displayed.

    • isPoweredByText
      Type: Boolean
      Purpose: Indicates if a text-based “powered by” label should be shown.

    • loginOtpLength
      Type: Number
      Purpose: Defines the OTP length for general user login (e.g., 6).

    • pagesV2
      Type: Boolean
      Purpose: Indicates whether version 2 of the UI pages is in use.

    • preLoginInit
      Type: Boolean
      Purpose: If true, triggers pre-login initialization routines.

    • showAgentDashboard
      Type: Boolean
      Purpose: Controls the visibility of the agent dashboard.

    • stageData
      Type: Boolean
      Purpose: Indicates whether staged (or test) data should be used.

    • userJourney
      Type: Boolean
      Purpose: Enables tracking or customization of the user journey through the login process.

Conclusion

This configuration file is designed to offer a high degree of customization for your frontend login experience. It allows you to:

  • Define field behavior and validation for mobile login.

  • Support multiple languages and customize language options.

  • Control pre-fill behavior for login forms.

  • Configure privacy policy access and presentation.

  • Set up theming and branding with logos and color schemes.

  • Present terms & conditions dynamically.

  • Fine-tune miscellaneous behaviors via utility flags.

By understanding and adjusting these parameters, developers can ensure a flexible, user-friendly, and branded login process.

bodyMarkdown:
### Steps to Check Video Availability on RBL Server

Follow these steps to check and retrieve the required video files:

#### **Step 1: Access the RBL Server**

- Connect to the RBL server at **.62** (Ubuntu).

#### **Step 2: Start the Environment**

- Run the command:

  ```bash
  startenv
  ```

#### **Step 3: Create and Edit Required Files**

- Open the `user_ids.txt` file and enter user IDs (one per line):

  ```bash
  vi user_ids.txt
  ```

- Open the `session_ids.txt` file and enter session IDs (one per line):

  ```bash
  vi session_ids.txt
  ```

  **Note:** Ensure that each session ID corresponds exactly to its respective user ID on the same line.

#### **Step 4: Run the Script**

- Execute the Python script to check video availability:

  ```bash
  python RBL_check_video_v1.py
  ```

#### **Step 5: Review the Output**

- The script will generate a CSV file as output.
  [![enter image description here](https://stackoverflowteams.com/c/kwikid/images/s/4fae0194-dda5-453e-bcf7-fce25e5c4b9c.png)](https://stackoverflowteams.com/c/kwikid/images/s/4fae0194-dda5-453e-bcf7-fce25e5c4b9c.png)

- Download the CSV file for further analysis.
  [![enter image description here](https://stackoverflowteams.com/c/kwikid/images/s/06f348c7-4045-4887-94b4-2a390745689d.png)](https://stackoverflowteams.com/c/kwikid/images/s/06f348c7-4045-4887-94b4-2a390745689d.png)

#### **Output Explanation**

- The output will indicate whether the required video files are present.
- **Legend for Output Values:**
  - **1** → Video is present.
  - **0** → Video is not present.

#### **Important Notes**

- Only the `agent_video_screen.webm` file can be recovered.
- If the other two video files show `0`, they are **non-recoverable** (i.e., they were never generated or stored in the S3 bucket).

---

This version improves clarity, structure, and readability, making it more user-friendly. Let me know if you need any further refinements! 🚀

title: How to Execute the Aadhaar PDF Recovery Script for CBI?
bodyMarkdown: How to Execute the Aadhaar PDF Recovery Script for CBI ?
body: How to Execute the Aadhaar PDF Recovery Script for CBI ?

bodyMarkdown:
Server :- cbi.vkyc.getkwikid.com

cd /home/ubuntu/script

source ../venv-dkyc/bin/activate

### Prerequisites

1. Python 3.6+ installed

2. AWS CLI configured with the `dkycuat-minio` profile

3. The `boto3` Python package installed

4. Access to required S3 buckets and DynamoDB tables

### Step 1: Create a File with User IDs

Create a text file named `user_ids.txt` with one user ID per line:

vi user_ids.txt 

```
8797513665
9078229339
9058125209
8770881263
# Add more user IDs as needed
```

save 

### Step 3: Run the Script

Execute the script using one of the following methods:

#### For a single user:

```
python recover_aadhaar_pdf.py --user-ids 9078229339 --profile dkycuat-minio
```

#### For multiple users (from command line):

```
python recover_aadhaar_pdf.py --user-ids 9078229339 7717791007 8797513665 --profile dkycuat-minio
```

#### For processing users from a file:

```
python recover_aadhaar_pdf.py --input-file user_ids.txt --profile dkycuat-minio
```

### Step 4: Check the Results

After execution, the script will:

1. Print progress for each user

2. Show which files were found and copied

3. Generate a summary of successes and failures

4. Create a file called `aadhaar_recovery_results.txt` with detailed results

### Troubleshooting

#### SSL Warnings

If you see SSL warnings, they can be safely ignored as the script already has SSL verification disabled.

#### 403 Forbidden Errors

Ensure your AWS credentials in the `dkycuat-minio` profile have the correct permissions to access the S3 bucket and DynamoDB table.

#### Missing XML Files

The script looks for both PDF and XML files. If XML files don't exist, the script will still try to recover the PDF files.

### Example Output

Successful execution should show output like:

```
Processing user: 9078229339
Session 0dbdd777-b8a4-427b-8496-02581a645877:
DynamoDB PDF URL: https://vkyc.centralbank.co.in/v1/download_content/kwikid/videokyc/summary/CBI/9078229339/0dbdd777-b8a4-427b-8496-02581a645877/aadhaar_redacted.pdf (Exists: False)
DynamoDB XML URL: None (Exists: False)
Found PDF at: videokyc/aadhaar/CBI/9078229339/9078229339_aadhaar_redacted.pdf
Found XML at: None
Copied PDF from videokyc/aadhaar/CBI/9078229339/9078229339_aadhaar_redacted.pdf to videokyc/summary/CBI/9078229339/0dbdd777-b8a4-427b-8496-02581a645877/aadhaar_redacted.pdf
Successfully updated documents for user 9078229339
```

### Additional Options

The script supports these additional command-line options:

- `--batch-size` - Number of users to process in each batch (default: 50)

- You can modify the script to support other client names or bucket names as needed

### Notes

- This script is specifically configured for the CBI environment

- It uses the S3 endpoint URL: `https://mio.vkyc.cbi.dc.getkwikid.com`

- It uses the DynamoDB endpoint URL: `https://db.vkyc.cbi.dc.getkwikid.com`

- The script updates URLs to use the format: `https://vkyc.centralbank.co.in/v1/download_content/kwikid/...`

source ../venv-dkyc/bin/activate

Prerequisites

  1. Python 3.6+ installed

  2. AWS CLI configured with the dkycuat-minio profile

  3. The boto3 Python package installed

  4. Access to required S3 buckets and DynamoDB tables

Step 1: Create a File with User IDs

Create a text file named user_ids.txt with one user ID per line:

vi user_ids.txt

8797513665
9078229339
9058125209
8770881263
# Add more user IDs as needed

save

Step 3: Run the Script

Execute the script using one of the following methods:

For a single user:

python recover_aadhaar_pdf.py --user-ids 9078229339 --profile dkycuat-minio

For multiple users (from command line):

python recover_aadhaar_pdf.py --user-ids 9078229339 7717791007 8797513665 --profile dkycuat-minio

For processing users from a file:

python recover_aadhaar_pdf.py --input-file user_ids.txt --profile dkycuat-minio

Step 4: Check the Results

After execution, the script will:

  1. Print progress for each user

  2. Show which files were found and copied

  3. Generate a summary of successes and failures

  4. Create a file called aadhaar_recovery_results.txt with detailed results

Troubleshooting

SSL Warnings

If you see SSL warnings, they can be safely ignored as the script already has SSL verification disabled.

403 Forbidden Errors

Ensure your AWS credentials in the dkycuat-minio profile have the correct permissions to access the S3 bucket and DynamoDB table.

Missing XML Files

The script looks for both PDF and XML files. If XML files don't exist, the script will still try to recover the PDF files.

Example Output

Successful execution should show output like:

Processing user: 9078229339
Session 0dbdd777-b8a4-427b-8496-02581a645877:
DynamoDB PDF URL: https://vkyc.centralbank.co.in/v1/download_content/kwikid/videokyc/summary/CBI/9078229339/0dbdd777-b8a4-427b-8496-02581a645877/aadhaar_redacted.pdf (Exists: False)
DynamoDB XML URL: None (Exists: False)
Found PDF at: videokyc/aadhaar/CBI/9078229339/9078229339_aadhaar_redacted.pdf
Found XML at: None
Copied PDF from videokyc/aadhaar/CBI/9078229339/9078229339_aadhaar_redacted.pdf to videokyc/summary/CBI/9078229339/0dbdd777-b8a4-427b-8496-02581a645877/aadhaar_redacted.pdf
Successfully updated documents for user 9078229339

Additional Options

The script supports these additional command-line options:

  • --batch-size - Number of users to process in each batch (default: 50)

  • You can modify the script to support other client names or bucket names as needed

Notes

  • This script is specifically configured for the CBI environment

  • It uses the S3 endpoint URL: https://mio.vkyc.cbi.dc.getkwikid.com

  • It uses the DynamoDB endpoint URL: https://db.vkyc.cbi.dc.getkwikid.com

  • The script updates URLs to use the format: https://vkyc.centralbank.co.in/v1/download_content/kwikid/...

title: How to store redacted/masked data in DB?
bodyMarkdown: To store redacted data in our DB across all points, if needed. (Considering aadhaar_number in this scenario)
body: To store redacted data in our DB across all points, if needed. (Considering aadhaar_number in this scenario)

bodyMarkdown:
To implement this in the **userConfig** level for the user-forms where we ask for **aadhaar_number**, 

Refer following steps: -

1. The 'type' should be **text**

   [![enter image description here](https://stackoverflowteams.com/c/kwikid/images/s/9feec1be-7c4a-4106-bf53-f28bf64ce92f.png)](https://stackoverflowteams.com/c/kwikid/images/s/9feec1be-7c4a-4106-bf53-f28bf64ce92f.png)

2. Specify the 'validation' which triggers **ON_SAVE** method

   [![enter image description here](https://stackoverflowteams.com/c/kwikid/images/s/1bdc42d7-87ce-4472-96b3-e357f7daefd2.png)](https://stackoverflowteams.com/c/kwikid/images/s/1bdc42d7-87ce-4472-96b3-e357f7daefd2.png)

3. Create necessary rules and don't forget to specify this particular **SET_VALUE** action shown below which takes custom formula-based masking approach

   [![enter image description here](https://stackoverflowteams.com/c/kwikid/images/s/55458ffc-4428-4923-80c0-9ac8d8c2a347.png)](https://stackoverflowteams.com/c/kwikid/images/s/55458ffc-4428-4923-80c0-9ac8d8c2a347.png)

   This config would now accept the data in text format, and upon clicking SAVE or NEXT button in the form, it would trigger this *ON_SAVE* validation section which would mask the data and then store it in the *form_data* object.

Now, in the VKYC journey, where there could be a need to redact the data and store the redacted data in the DB, we have 2 keys in **agentConfig**: -

1. **isRedact**: This key redacts the data and stores in the redux. (**Please Note:** Not all the data variables across the DB are stored in the redacted format.)

2. **isRedactedInDb**: This key is used in the level of *isRedact* only, and works same as *isRedact* with the only difference being that, when it's **true**, it redacts the data from the *auditTrailData* as well and it helps in **completely storing** the **redacted data** in **DB**. 

Now, there are some particular instances where in the client wrapper APIs, we have to redact the data from backend. For eg: *kwikid-canara-wrapper* giving the redacted fields from */download_ckyc api*.

For this point, we mention the data fields we want to mask in the *env* file itself with the **MASKING_FIELDS** key

[![enter image description here](https://stackoverflowteams.com/c/kwikid/images/s/4a1ce45c-b746-4d70-9acf-2c3c2bbb004e.png)](https://stackoverflowteams.com/c/kwikid/images/s/4a1ce45c-b746-4d70-9acf-2c3c2bbb004e.png)

**Please note:** To add in more fields here for the backend, we have to make changes in the code for the same. The variables here help to decide if we want to redact particular fields mentioned in the .env file or not.
body:
To implement this in the userConfig level for the user-forms where we ask for aadhaar_number,

Refer following steps: -

  1. The 'type' should be text

  2. Specify the 'validation' which triggers ON_SAVE method

  3. Create necessary rules and don't forget to specify this particular SET_VALUE action shown below which takes custom formula-based masking approach

    This config would now accept the data in text format, and upon clicking SAVE or NEXT button in the form, it would trigger this ON_SAVE validation section which would mask the data and then store it in the form_data object.

Now, in the VKYC journey, where there could be a need to redact the data and store the redacted data in the DB, we have 2 keys in agentConfig: -

  1. isRedact: This key redacts the data and stores in the redux. (Please Note: Not all the data variables across the DB are stored in the redacted format.)

  2. isRedactedInDb: This key is used in the level of isRedact only, and works same as isRedact with the only difference being that, when it's true, it redacts the data from the auditTrailData as well and it helps in completely storing the redacted data in DB.

Now, there are some particular instances where in the client wrapper APIs, we have to redact the data from backend. For eg: kwikid-canara-wrapper giving the redacted fields from /download_ckyc api.

For this point, we mention the data fields we want to mask in the env file itself with the MASKING_FIELDS key

Please note: To add in more fields here for the backend, we have to make changes in the code for the same. The variables here help to decide if we want to redact particular fields mentioned in the .env file or not.

body: Troubleshooting Guide: Adding Missing PERSONAL_DETAILS Structure to DynamoDB Records | unity

bodyMarkdown:
Inshort:- 

Check the cbs_summary error and if it is regarding form_data issue. 

check for the traces and then take action. 

below is just one example on how it got resolved. 

cbs_summary error is :- 

```
        "cbs_summary": "{\"global_unhandled_exception\": \"Traceback (most recent call last):\\n  File \\\"/home/ubuntu/Kwikid_ipv_poc/kwikid_celery_tasks/cbs.py\\\", line 142, in cbs_init\\n    cbs_data = cbs_request(user_id, session_id, client_name, productCode, cust_id, **data)\\n  File \\\"/home/ubuntu/Kwikid_ipv_poc/kwikid_celery_tasks/cbs.py\\\", line 57, in cbs_request\\n    risk, risk_response = calculate_risk(_USER_ID, _SESSION_ID, _CLIENT_NAME, _PRODUCT_CODE, form_data)\\n  File \\\"/home/ubuntu/Kwikid_ipv_poc/kwikid_celery_tasks/app/risk.py\\\", line 10, in calculate_risk\\n    annual_income = data[\\\"PERSONAL_DETAILS\\\"][\\\"gross_annual_income\\\"].replace(\\\",\\\", \\\"\\\").strip()\\nKeyError: 'PERSONAL_DETAILS'\\n\", \"failure_reason\": \"global_unhandled_exception\"}",
```

## Description

We encountered an error in our risk calculation function when processing customer data:

```
KeyError: 'PERSONAL_DETAILS'
```

The function was trying to access `data["PERSONAL_DETAILS"]["father_spouse_full_name"]`, but the `PERSONAL_DETAILS` key didn't exist in the form_data structure in DynamoDB.

## Investigation Steps

1. First, we checked the DynamoDB record structure to understand what was missing:

   ```
   aws dynamodb get-item --table-name kwikid_customer_form_data --key '{"customer_id": {"S": "8438274300"}, "transaction_id": {"S": "8438274300_931c3795-2035-478b-a65a-9329d9d09377"}}'
   
   ```

2. We found that while the form_data contained `BASIC_DETAILS` and `PERSONAL_INFORMATION`, it was missing the required `PERSONAL_DETAILS` structure.

3. We discovered that the required PERSONAL_DETAILS information was available in an `extras` field as a JSON string, but was not structured in the form that the risk calculation function expected.

## Solution Approach Evolution

### First Attempt (Failed)

We initially tried using a document path update expression to add just the PERSONAL_DETAILS field:

```
# This failed with a ValidationException
dynamodb.update_item(
    TableName='kwikid_customer_form_data',
    Key={
        'customer_id': {'S': customer_id},
        'transaction_id': {'S': transaction_id}
    },
    UpdateExpression='SET form_data.M.PERSONAL_DETAILS = :pd',
    ExpressionAttributeValues={
        ':pd': personal_details_map
    }
)
```

The error we received was:

```
An error occurred (ValidationException) when calling the UpdateItem operation: The document path provided in the update expression is invalid for update
```

This happened because the DynamoDB document path syntax couldn't correctly navigate the nested structure of our form_data.

### Final Solution (Successful)

Our successful approach involved:

1. Retrieving the entire record

2. Creating a clone of the form_data structure

3. Adding the PERSONAL_DETAILS field to the appropriate location in the structure

4. Replacing the entire form_data field with our modified version

```
# Clone the form_data and add PERSONAL_DETAILS
new_form_data = dict(form_data)

# Add PERSONAL_DETAILS to the appropriate location
if 'M' in new_form_data:
    new_form_data['M']['PERSONAL_DETAILS'] = personal_details_map
else:
    new_form_data['PERSONAL_DETAILS'] = personal_details_map

# Update the entire form_data
dynamodb.update_item(
    TableName='kwikid_customer_form_data',
    Key={
        'customer_id': {'S': customer_id},
        'transaction_id': {'S': transaction_id}
    },
    UpdateExpression='SET form_data = :fd',
    ExpressionAttributeValues={
        ':fd': new_form_data
    }
)
```

## Python Script

Here's the final script we created to add the PERSONAL_DETAILS structure:

```
import json
import boto3
import sys

def update_form_data(customer_id, transaction_id):
    # Initialize DynamoDB client
    dynamodb = boto3.client('dynamodb')
    
    # First, get the existing item
    try:
        response = dynamodb.get_item(
            TableName='kwikid_customer_form_data',
            Key={
                'customer_id': {'S': customer_id},
                'transaction_id': {'S': transaction_id}
            }
        )
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Error retrieving item: {e}")
        return False
    
    if 'Item' not in response:
        print(f"Item not found for customer_id={customer_id}, transaction_id={transaction_id}")
        return False
    
    item = response['Item']
    print("Retrieved item from DynamoDB")
    
    # Check if form_data exists
    if 'form_data' in item:
        form_data = item['form_data']
        
        # Create a complete PERSONAL_DETAILS structure
        personal_details_map = {
            'M': {
                'gross_annual_income': {'S': '5,00,000 - 10,00,000'},
                'marital_status': {'S': 'Married'},
                'education': {'S': 'Under Graduate'},
                'occupation': {'S': 'Retired'},
                'source_of_income': {'S': 'Pension'},
                'father_spouse_full_name': {'S': 'K SAMPATH'},
                'mother_name': {'S': 'K SHANTHI'},
                'occupation_mapping': {'S': 'retired'},
                'terms_and_conditions_checkbox': {'BOOL': True},
                'fatca_agreement_checkbox': {'BOOL': True},
                'combined_osg': {'S': 'Occupation: Retired, Source of Income: Pension, Gross Annual Income: 5,00,000 - 10,00,000'}
            }
        }
        
        # Clone the form_data and add PERSONAL_DETAILS
        new_form_data = dict(form_data)
        
        # Add PERSONAL_DETAILS to the appropriate location
        if 'M' in new_form_data:
            new_form_data['M']['PERSONAL_DETAILS'] = personal_details_map
        else:
            new_form_data['PERSONAL_DETAILS'] = personal_details_map
        
        # Update the entire form_data
        try:
            dynamodb.update_item(
                TableName='kwikid_customer_form_data',
                Key={
                    'customer_id': {'S': customer_id},
                    'transaction_id': {'S': transaction_id}
                },
                UpdateExpression='SET form_data = :fd',
                ExpressionAttributeValues={
                    ':fd': new_form_data
                }
            )
            print(f"Successfully updated form_data with complete PERSONAL_DETAILS for customer_id={customer_id}")
            return True
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"Update attempt failed: {e}")
            return False
    else:
        print("form_data not found in Item")
        return False

if __name__ == "__main__":
    if len(sys.argv) != 3:
        print("Usage: python update_form_data.py <customer_id> <transaction_id>")
        sys.exit(1)
    
    customer_id = sys.argv[1]
    transaction_id = sys.argv[2]
    
    success = update_form_data(customer_id, transaction_id)
    if success:
        print("Update completed successfully")
    else:
        print("Update failed")
```

## Execution Steps

1. Save the script as `update_form_data.py`

2. Run the script with the customer_id and transaction_id:

   ```
   python update_form_data.py 8438274300 8438274300_931c3795-2035-478b-a65a-9329d9d09377
   
   ```

3. Verify the update was successful:

   ```
   aws dynamodb get-item --table-name kwikid_customer_form_data --key '{"customer_id": {"S": "8438274300"}, "transaction_id": {"S": "8438274300_931c3795-2035-478b-a65a-9329d9d09377"}}'
   
   ```

## Key Learnings

1. **Understanding DynamoDB Document Paths**: When using update expressions with document paths (like `form_data.M.PERSONAL_DETAILS`), we encountered limitations. These paths don't always work as expected with deeply nested attributes.

2. **Whole Object Replacement**: For complex nested structures, sometimes it's cleaner to retrieve the entire object, modify it in memory, and then replace it as a whole.

3. **DynamoDB Structure Sensitivity**: The DynamoDB JSON structure is very specific with its type markers (like "S" for string, "M" for map). When creating new elements, we had to ensure they matched the expected format.

4. **Progressive Debugging**: We used a step-by-step approach, first checking what was in the database, then trying one update approach, and when that failed, switching to an alternative approach.

## For Future Issues

If you encounter similar issues with DynamoDB updates:

1. Use the AWS CLI to examine the exact structure of your records

2. Be cautious with document path expressions for deeply nested attributes

3. Consider the "clone-modify-replace" pattern for complex updates

4. Always include good error handling to understand what's failing

title: Creating Users (Maker/Checker) in CBI's DKYC
bodyMarkdown: We have to register maker/checker for CBI's DKYC journey.
body: We have to register maker/checker for CBI's DKYC journey.

bodyMarkdown:
```
curl --location 'https://dkycuat.centralbank.co.in/v1/agent/signup' \
--header 'Accept: application/json' \
--header 'Accept-Language: en-GB,en-US;q=0.9,en;q=0.8' \
--header 'Cache-Control: no-cache' \
--header 'Connection: keep-alive' \
--header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
--data '{
    "agent_id": "130165",
    "is_agent": true,
    "is_auditor": false
}'
```

Use the above curl to register user on DKYC. Load it into Postman and get started.

Here, the only requirements (provided by the client) are,  
1\. agent_id (should be available in the Client's HRMS)  
2\. is_agent, is_auditor  
(for **maker**, is_agent = true & is_auditor = false  
for **checker**, is_agent = false & is_auditor = true)

For UAT, url should be https://dkycuat.centralbank.co.in/v1/agent/signup  
For PROD, url should be <https://dkyc.centralbank.co.in/v1/agent/signup>

P.S.  
1\. In CBI's DKYC, Password is not set, since there's AD integration.  
2\. API is dependent on Client's HRMS API. Fields being pulled from it are, branch_code, branch_name, mobile, name

title: How to create CSR File for SSL certificate
bodyMarkdown: How to create CSR File for SSL certificate
body: How to create CSR File for SSL certificate

bodyMarkdown:
Go to auat server (can go to any server ideally where openssl is installed)

cd /home/ubuntu/csrfiles/csrfold2/\<client_name_MM_YY\>

openssl genrsa -out private.key 2048

openssl req -new -key private.key -out server.csr

 OpenSSL will prompt you for below details, including: 

- Country Name (C) \<IN\>

- State or Province Name (ST) \<Enter Company's HO State Name\>

- Locality Name (L) \<City Name\>

- Organization Name (O) \<Org Name EG: CANARA BANK\>

- Organizational Unit Name (OU) \<IT DEPT\>

- Common Name (CN) (usually the domain name for web servers) \<Enter the domain name here for which csr file is required eg: uatvideokyclc.canarabank.com\>

- Email Address: optional, leave it empty

- Optional attributes: Challenge password and company name (can be left blank): Optional, leave it empty.

Submit.

**\*NOTE: DO NOT SHARE PRIVATE.KEY to CLIENT AT ANY COST\*  Just share the server.csr file**

title: How to monitor server space, CPU, and disk usage and status of Docker containers and services?
bodyMarkdown:
**SOP for setting up the script in any server will be as follows**

 1. Save the script in a file named **monitoring.sh** at location (**/home/ubuntu/monitoring/**).  
    Script details:  
     

    ```
    #!/bin/bash
    
    ######################################
    # Editable Fields (Modify as Needed) #
    ######################################
    
    # Define threshold values for alerts
    cpu_threshold=85         # CPU usage threshold in percentage
    memory_threshold=75      # Memory usage threshold in percentage
    disk_threshold=75        # Disk usage threshold in percentage
    
    # Define lists of Docker containers and system services to monitor
    # Add container names if needed (Example: containers=("container1" "container2"))
    containers=()
    
    # Add service names if needed (Example: services=("service1.service" "service2.service"))
    services=()
    
    # URL for Kuma (or any monitoring tool) webhook notification (Leave empty if not used)
    kuma_url=""
    
    #############################################
    #############################################
    
    status="up"
    message="OK"
    non_running_containers=""
    non_running_services=""
    
    # Get current CPU usage
    cpu_usage=$(top -bn1 | grep "Cpu(s)" | sed "s/.*, *\([0-9.]*\)%* id.*/\1/" | awk '{print int(100 - $1)}')
    
    # Get current memory usage
    memory_usage=$(free | grep Mem | awk '{print int($3/$2 * 100.0)}')
    
    # Get main disk (root `/`) usage
    main_disk_usage=$(df / | grep / | awk '{print int($5)}')
    
    # Check if specified Docker containers are running
    for container in "${containers[@]}"; do
        if [[ $(docker inspect --format '{{.State.Running}}' $container 2> /dev/null) != "true" ]]; then
            echo "Container '$container' is not running."
            non_running_containers+="$container-"
        else
            echo "Container '$container' is running."
        fi
    done
    
    # Check if specified system services are active
    for service in "${services[@]}"; do
        if [[ $(systemctl is-active "$service") == "active" || $(systemctl is-active "$service") == "activating" ]]; then
            echo "Service '$service' is running."
        else
            echo "Service '$service' is not running."
            non_running_services+="$service-"
        fi
    done
    
    # Check if CPU usage exceeds the threshold
    if [[ "$cpu_usage" -gt $cpu_threshold ]]; then
        if [[ "$message" == "OK" ]]; then
            message=""
        fi
        status="down"
        message+="CPU:$cpu_usage%-"
    fi
    
    # Check if memory usage exceeds the threshold
    if [ "$memory_usage" -gt $memory_threshold ]; then
        if [[ "$message" == "OK" ]]; then
            message=""
        fi
        status="down"
        message+="Memory:$memory_usage%-"
    fi
    
    # Check if disk usage exceeds the threshold
    if [ "$main_disk_usage" -gt $disk_threshold ]; then
        if [[ "$message" == "OK" ]]; then
            message=""
        fi
        status="down"
        message+="Disk:$main_disk_usage%-"
    fi
    
    # Append non-running container details to message
    if [ -n "$non_running_containers" ]; then
        if [[ "$message" == "OK" ]]; then
            message=""
        fi
        status="down"
        message+="Container:$non_running_containers"
    fi
    
    # Append non-running service details to message
    if [ -n "$non_running_services" ]; then
        if [[ "$message" == "OK" ]]; then
            message=""
        fi
        status="down"
        message+="Service:$non_running_services"
    fi
    
    # Print monitoring results
    echo "CPU Usage: $cpu_usage%"
    echo "Memory Usage: $memory_usage%"
    echo "Main Disk Usage: $main_disk_usage%"
    echo "Status: $status"
    echo "Message: $message"
    
    # Send alert using Kuma monitoring webhook (if configured)
    curl "$kuma_url?status=$status&msg=$message"
    
    ```

 2. Make the file executable by running the command

    1. chmod +x \<absolute_file_location\> for example   
       **chmod +x** **/home/ubuntu/monitoring/monitoring.sh**

 3. Finalize the threshold value of the CPU Usage and set the same value in the **cpu_threshold** variable.

 4. Finalize the threshold value of the Memory Usage and set the same value in the **memory_threshold** variable.

 5. Finalize the threshold value of the Disk Usage and set the same value in the **disk_threshold** variable.

 6. Note down the names of the concerned containers for which monitoring is to be enabled and set the names in the **containers** variable as space separated value.

    1. for instance there are two containers for which the monitoring has to be enabled namely a and b then the value of the containers variable will look like this. **containers=("a" "b")**

 7. Note down the names of the concerned **services** for which monitoring is to be enabled and set the names in the services variable as space separated value.

    1. for instance there are two services for which the monitoring has to be enabled namely a.service and b.service then the value of the services variable will look like this. **services=("a.service" "b.service")**

 8. Finalize the creation of Monitor on Uptime Kuma and then copy its PUSH KUMA URL and set just the base url in the kuma_url value, for example ([http://status.getkwikid.com:3001/api/push/ViGCQuhHTf](http://status.getkwikid.com:3001/api/push/ViGCQuhHTf?status=up&msg=OK&ping=)).

    [![enter image description here](https://stackoverflowteams.com/c/kwikid/images/s/18b2ae4d-52c1-43eb-811c-620bdea5ae16.png)](https://stackoverflowteams.com/c/kwikid/images/s/18b2ae4d-52c1-43eb-811c-620bdea5ae16.png)

    [![enter image description here](https://stackoverflowteams.com/c/kwikid/images/s/d8d5f261-3653-4f6a-9a6c-ee53ec483a37.png)](https://stackoverflowteams.com/c/kwikid/images/s/d8d5f261-3653-4f6a-9a6c-ee53ec483a37.png)

 9. Confirm the working of the underlying commands by running sample commands mentioned below

    1. top -version

    2. free --version

    3. df --version

    4. docker --version

10. Schedule a cronjob by running the command crontab -e, set the cronjob as per required time (every minute is recommended), save the file and exit. for example **\* \* \* \* \* /home/ubuntu/monitoring/monitoring.sh**

If all of the above steps mentioned are followed as instructed then all the commands written will work as expected, resulting in completion of script and reporting the status to Kuma.

  7. Note down the names of the concerned services for which monitoring is to be enabled and set the names in the services variable as space separated value.

    1. for instance there are two services for which the monitoring has to be enabled namely a.service and b.service then the value of the services variable will look like this. services=("a.service" "b.service")

  8. Finalize the creation of Monitor on Uptime Kuma and then copy its PUSH KUMA URL and set just the base url in the kuma_url value, for example (http://status.getkwikid.com:3001/api/push/ViGCQuhHTf).

  9. Confirm the working of the underlying commands by running sample commands mentioned below

    1. top -version

    2. free --version

    3. df --version

    4. docker --version

  10. Schedule a cronjob by running the command crontab -e, set the cronjob as per required time (every minute is recommended), save the file and exit. for example * * * * * /home/ubuntu/monitoring/monitoring.sh

If all of the above steps mentioned are followed as instructed then all the commands written will work as expected, resulting in completion of script and reporting the status to Kuma.

You can use the below code that send the url msg ---\> uptime dashboard which will show you the live percentage  
  
1.disk-usage 

```
#unity ML -server 
#!/bin/bash

# Uptime Kuma's unique URL for your monitor
KUMA_URL="<add the kuma url here>"

# Function to URL encode parameters
urlencode() {
    local length="${#1}"
    for (( i = 0; i < length; i++ )); do
        local c="${1:i:1}"
        case $c in
            [a-zA-Z0-9.~_-]) printf "$c" ;;
            *) printf '%%%02X' "'$c" ;;
        esac
    done
}

# Check disk usage
disk_space=$(df -h / | awk 'NR==2 {print $5}' | sed 's/%//')

# Set initial status and message
status="up"
msg="Disk usage is OK (${disk_space}%)"

# Check if disk usage is greater than 85
if [ "$disk_space" -gt 85 ]; then
  status="down"
  msg="Disk space critical (${disk_space}%)"
fi

echo "Final Status: $status"
echo "Final Msg: $msg"

# URL encode the status and message
encoded_status=$(urlencode "$status")
encoded_msg=$(urlencode "$msg")

# Push the status and message to Uptime Kuma
curl -X GET "$KUMA_URL?status=$encoded_status&msg=$encoded_msg"

body:
Problem Statement

Unity reported an issue where the aadhaar_reference_number field was blank in CBS callback logs for user ID 8140308899, even though the Aadhaar number itself was visible in their system.

bodyMarkdown:
## Issue

Unity reported missing `aadhaar_reference_number` in callback logs for user 8140308899, while it was present for user 9664130157.

**Ticket:** CB | P0 | PROD | Unity : Aadhar ref no. field is blank in CBS

## Root Cause

This is expected behavior due to different journey types:

- User 8140308899: **VKYC journey** - we receive aadhaar_reference_number from partners
- User 9664130157: **NTB journey** - we fetch aadhaar_reference_number from Aadhaar vault API

## Resolution

Informed client that:

1. In VKYC journeys: Partners provide the aadhaar_reference_number
2. In NTB journeys: We get the aadhaar_reference_number from Aadhaar vault API

## Note for Support

When troubleshooting missing fields in callbacks, always check the user's journey type as available fields differ between journeys.

Asana Ticket Link:-  [CB | P0 | PROD | Unity : Aadhar ref no. field is blank in CBS](https://app.asana.com/1/1200709063324892/project/1206726066125543/task/1209975719673055?focus=true)

bodyMarkdown:
it is for general purpose 

this aws cmd will help you when you didn't know the key or table and you want to find it 

```
aws dynamodb get-item \
--table-name kwikid_vkyc_session_status \
--key '{"session_id": {"S": "your-session-id-here"}}' \
--endpoint-url https://db.vkyc.cbi.dc.getkwikid.com --no-verify-ssl
```

**What it does:**

- It **fetches** (retrieves) **one record** (one item) from the DynamoDB table `kwikid_vkyc_session_status`.

- It searches using the **primary key** (`session_id`).

- It will **print** the full details (all columns/fields) of that session ID.

now 

Here's the **AWS CLI command** you should run to update `audit_result` to rejected:

```
aws dynamodb update-item \
--table-name kwikid_vkyc_session_status \
--key '{"session_id": {"S": "93a30599-28a9-4a0e-9828-5aeb2d109261"}}' \
--update-expression "SET audit_result = :val" \
--expression-attribute-values '{":val": {"N": "0"}}' \
--endpoint-url https://db.vkyc.cbi.dc.getkwikid.com --no-verify-ssl
```

if you want to approve then make "val" 0 to 1
